# HyperAI Monorepo State Slices

Every code or data mutation names one slice. Local validation, source
provenance, external review, external effects, and production authorization
remain distinct evidence and authority gates.

## `hyperai.bazaar_interface_plan.v1`

Status: active documentation refinement; no product implementation or
external authority is granted.

Purpose: define the end-to-end HyperAI product and architecture plan for
composing Bazaar-inspired market research, data, fleet, and evaluation
workflows with the buyer, seller, inference, evidence, and settlement roles of
the adjacent systems. HyperAI is the product interface; its modules and
connected systems retain their own records, runtimes, credentials, and
authority. The plan's north star is a buyer-controlled batch-inference and
evaluation journey from workload description and supply comparison through
quote approval, authorized execution, evaluation, and a portable receipt. The
bounded market-owned workload identity and synthetic read-only trace are
implemented. Served browser evidence now includes fixed seller-failure and
inconclusive mock-outcome previews, plus owner-backed local Data outcomes for
one synthetic snapshot. The signed seller-failure record is already served by
an owner-only route and browser preview; its fixed read-only projection is also
available through an opt-in CLI flag, TUI controls, and an append-only MCP V3
tool. The default CLI and MCP V1/V2 contracts remain compatible, and ACP stays
read-only. Remaining local gaps include broad accessibility, cross-browser
behavior, and full client-policy parity beyond the focused preview tests. The
report is synthetic and does not establish real execution, failure, refund, or
payment entitlement.
The first complete walkthrough remains local, synthetic, and mock-only. The
plan makes connection maturity visible (HyperAI local, offline source record,
reference only, separately authorized adapter, optional projection) and
defines task-based usability evidence for navigation, provenance, lifecycle,
and action previews without creating a second ledger.

This refinement records the bounded procurement decision: `hyperai-market`
owns `WorkloadIntentV1` for the local trace, while general workload identity
outside procurement remains open. The versioned intent and read-only
application projection are implemented without changing existing V1 market
contracts. The critical-path table distinguishes implemented local
capabilities from the remaining workflow, usability, accessibility, and
client-policy qualification, so separate local modules are not presented as a
fully qualified product journey. The current-position summary reflects the
owner-backed Data read and seller-failure client follow-up and preserves the
distinction between seller-reported failure and verifier rejection/refund.
This refinement also adds a concise refactor brief
with the source-role map, end-to-end buyer path, build order, visual and
usability acceptance, and owner-specific gates. It makes the existing HyperAI
browser shell the first integrated surface and leaves browser versus packaged
desktop as a measured product decision rather than adding a parallel runtime.
The bounded `hyperai-market` ownership decision is implemented under
`hyperai.bazaar.workload_trace_synthetic.v1`; it does not authorize a general
cross-product identity, external connections, or other effects.

2026-10-01 refinement: the interface plan now has a concise program roadmap
for preserving owner boundaries, composing the existing HyperAI surface,
qualifying one synthetic buyer journey, linking adjacent workspaces through
owner references, finishing client/usability qualification, and gating live
adapters and settlement separately. The detailed phase sequence still tracks
the shared shell, synthetic supply and Data, buyer journey, offline HyperIntel
evidence, operator workspaces, experience/client parity, owner-approved
connections, and settlement. It marks existing local wiring separately from
remaining qualification, keeps the Data worker `NOT_ASSIGNED`, and identifies
the next milestone as one qualified buyer path across the existing clients.
This is documentation-only and grants no implementation or external-effect
authority.

2026-10-02 refinement: the plan now spells out the install-to-launch-to-
connection journey and groups navigation by user work (Work, Research, and
Operate), while keeping source ownership visible in the inspector and linked
records. It distinguishes static inventory from live health, makes local and
offline modes the default, and defines connection setup, revocation, loss, and
ACP limits. Current installed-path evidence is labeled macOS arm64 local
qualification only (macOS 26.6.1 arm64); platform, accessibility,
client-parity, and release gates remain open. This planning refinement
authorizes no connector, credential access, network request, product-code
change, or external effect.

2026-10-02 wiring audit refinement: source inspection confirms that the browser,
CLI, TUI, and ACP/MCP paths already converge on the authenticated local service
and `hyperai-application` facade, with ACP/MCP retaining its narrower scoped
read-only capability. It also identifies duplicated route knowledge across
the service router, agent route policy, MCP tool bridge, browser, CLI, and TUI.
The plan now sequences a complete route/auth/effect inventory and compatibility
checks before deciding whether a machine-readable contract or small typed
Rust client would materially reduce drift. This is a planning finding, not a
runtime defect or authorization to change existing API paths, schemas,
authentication, or client authority.

2026-10-02 end-to-end refactor refresh: `docs/bazaar-hyperai-interface-plan.md`
now presents a five-stage execution order: shared route/client compatibility,
the synthetic buyer journey, cross-workspace product and accessibility
qualification, owner-approved read adapters, then separately authorized
actions and settlement. It names route/auth/effect inventory plus synthetic
journey parity as the next milestone and defines “beautiful” through task
clarity, provenance, ownership, uncertainty, and accessible equivalents. This
is a planning refinement only; it authorizes no implementation, source reuse,
connection, credential access, or external effect.

Included files:

- `docs/bazaar-hyperai-interface-plan.md`: product decision, module map,
  integration contracts, UX direction, phased plan, acceptance gates, and
  assurance limits.
- `docs/compute-market-refactor-plan.md`: market contract plan and the
  bounded procurement workload-identity decision, while preserving existing

- `docs/state-slices.md`: this documentation-only authorization record.

Allowed effects: inspect the ignored local Bazaar reference and existing
HyperAI documentation; create or edit these Markdown planning records only.

Non-goals: copying Bazaar code, schemas, datasets, benchmark fixtures, visual
assets, or generated output; adding Bazaar to a build graph; changing product
workspaces; calling providers, agents, fleet APIs, SSH, wallets, or chains;
running evaluations; publishing evidence; or authorizing a future phase.

Claim ceiling: architecture plan based on the local README/architecture
reference and existing HyperAI repository records. Bazaar reuse rights,

Proof gates: confirm the pinned-source identity from existing provenance; keep
Bazaar ignored and untracked; record rights as unresolved; make each future
integration separately gated; keep every client on the shared facade and
module-owned contracts; state the design/usability acceptance tasks without
claiming they have passed; check current-position labels against the current
workspace and owner state-slice records; preserve the implemented bounded
procurement intent and existing V1 schemas, and keep general workload identity
outside procurement explicitly open; make the first implementation
path reuse the current shell and avoid a second runtime; do not attribute the
unversioned local `LICENSE` file to the pinned source; and pass Markdown diff
hygiene checks.

Settlement-rail refinement: the interface and compute-market plans now name
HyperEVM as the intended future EVM escrow rail for paid compute, while
keeping current settlement local and mock-only. Alkahest is recorded as a
candidate requiring deployment, dependency, and verifier-configuration
verification; no compatible HyperEVM deployment is assumed. The deal-binding
fields, offchain-verifier trust assumption, and read-only event/finality
receipt are explicit. This is planning evidence only and authorizes no chain
connection, wallet use, contract deployment, testnet write, paid execution,
or production operation.

## `hyperai.bazaar.interface.browser_process_state_diagnostic.v1`

Status: completed local diagnostic and narrowly scoped cleanup-parser
continuation. It does not reopen ACP cancellation browser identities v1-v4.

Purpose: preserve process-state evidence when the local ACP browser runner
checks its detached Chrome process group. A process group containing only
defunct (`Z`) processes has no executing member; report those PIDs separately
and consider the browser execution scope empty only when no non-defunct group
member remains for the existing stable-empty interval. The v4 packet did not
retain `ps` state, so a zombie-only group is a hypothesis, not an established
cause of that result.

Baseline: HyperAI `dcf41e31aa1f98438a6f8ec6cb253801e26dc0aa` on `main`, with
the pre-existing dirty and untracked work preserved. Frozen inputs before this
slice: `scripts/verify-interface-browser.mjs` (149,833 bytes; SHA-256
`70e43ba4ff7eecb7bb7aea97a27d42a3ac3b178213ceb152c78495e377d8c1bd`),
`package.json` (6,653 bytes; SHA-256
`c83c2a132cecaa471e5fcd0d98bfa28f62855cd6b61af45d877d16051e4ba2c8`), and
the read-only v4 record `docs/compute-bazaar-interface-acp-cancel-keyboard-v4-packet.md`
(8,848 bytes; SHA-256
`575abb7ff48ae7354c617f854270a14cc2c75f5e20a7ef0fd94865139aec7b06`).
The v4 packet remains unchanged.

Exact writable files:

- `scripts/verify-interface-browser.mjs`: consume process-state-aware group
  membership and report live and defunct PIDs separately.
- `scripts/browser-process-group.mjs`: parse fixed `ps` output and expose the
  process-group membership policy for the runner.
- `scripts/tests/browser-process-group.test.mjs`: fixed synthetic process
  table cases only.
- `package.json`: add the new pure JavaScript contract test to
  `verify:interface`.
- `docs/compute-bazaar-interface-cleanup-diagnostic-packet.md`: this packet's
  scope and evidence.
- `docs/compute-bazaar-rust-port-subplan.md` and
  `docs/bazaar-hyperai-interface-plan.md`: concise status and claim-limit
  references.
- `docs/state-slices.md`: this authorization and result.

Allowed effects: implement a deterministic parser over supplied `ps` text;
run its fixed synthetic unit cases, JavaScript syntax checks, the root fast
lint, root contract tests, import preservation, and diff hygiene. The parser
tests do not invoke `ps`, spawn children, open sockets, launch Chrome or the
HyperAI service, inspect live process tables, signal processes, or remove
temporary state. Do not run ACP cancellation browser identity v1, v2, v3, or
v4, and do not touch port `127.0.0.1:4317`. Do not repeat the prior full root
test suite until the recorded `HomeBusy` failure has a separate supported
diagnosis.

Non-goals: changing the ACP protocol, browser journey, app, service, MCP,
fixtures, process-group ownership model, signal grace periods, network policy,
or temporary-data policy; diagnosing the specific v4 process after it has
exited; or claiming full ACP cleanup qualification.

Threat model: `ps` output includes dead process-table entries that cannot
execute or retain file descriptors. Counting those entries as active can
misclassify cleanup. Conversely, a live or stopped non-defunct member must
remain a cleanup failure and must not be hidden by the parser.

Proof gates: fixed Darwin/Linux-style process-state rows parse into exact PID,
PGID, and state values; only a group with no non-defunct members is treated
as execution-empty; live, stopped, and unknown states remain active; malformed
rows are ignored without matching another PGID; JavaScript syntax and
`verify:interface` pass; root fast lint and contracts pass; import trees and
read-only v4 bytes remain unchanged; Markdown links and `git diff --check`
pass.

Claim ceiling: tested local interpretation of fixed synthetic `ps` text only.
It does not establish that v4 actually observed a zombie, that any Chrome
process was cleaned up, or that the browser cancellation workflow passes.
Assurance is `INTERNAL_PASS` only for the parser contract if its tests pass;
reviewer status is `NOT_REQUESTED`; reproduction is `NOT_REPRODUCED`. Browser
cleanup qualification remains `INCONCLUSIVE` pending a fresh separately
frozen workflow packet.

Publish boundary: local source and documentation only. No commit, PR, release,
external connection, process signal, or production action.

Implementation/evidence (2026-10-01): the shared process-group reader now
parses fixed PID, PGID, and `STAT` columns. Cleanup treats only `Z`/`Z+`
members as non-executing, retains live, stopped, and unknown states as active,
and emits the last runner-owned PID/state pairs in the ACP cleanup record.
Four fixed synthetic parser tests passed; `verify:interface`, root `lint:fast`,
root `verify:contracts`, import verification, browser-runner syntax,
linked-plan path checks, and `git diff --check` passed. Source hashes and
command details are in the [diagnostic packet](compute-bazaar-interface-cleanup-diagnostic-packet.md).

Assurance is `INTERNAL_PASS` for fixed process-table parser cases only.
Reviewer status is `NOT_REQUESTED`; reproduction is `NOT_REPRODUCED`. The
closed v4 packet is unchanged. Its cause remains unknown; this continuation
does not establish a browser cleanup pass. The `HomeBusy` root full-suite
failure remains uninvestigated and was not repeated. Next gate: a new frozen
browser workflow packet must use the diagnostic output before any browser
rerun; separately resolve the root `HomeBusy` failure before repeating
`verify:full`.

## `hyperai.bazaar.desk_runtime.storage_busy_diagnostic.v1`

Status: completed bounded diagnosis of one prior local full-suite failure;
the cause remains inconclusive. This is separate from the browser
process-state diagnostic and does not authorize repeating the full root suite.

Purpose: identify the exact call producing a prior `HomeBusy` error in
`storage::restore_failure_tests::failed_row_copy_rolls_back_and_reports_the_safety_backup`.
Current source shows `HomeBusy` can arise from the service lock or from
`backup_metadata` mapping an initialization-lock conflict; this test calls
the low-level restore helper and does not acquire the service lock. Add
test-only error context to its initialization and backup calls, then run only
the `hyperai-local-service` library unit-test target under normal parallel
libtest execution.

Baseline: HyperAI `dcf41e31aa1f98438a6f8ec6cb253801e26dc0aa` on `main`, with
all pre-existing dirty and untracked work preserved. The read-only starting
source `crates/hyperai-local-service/src/storage.rs` was 38,596 bytes at
SHA-256 `405ac552285fb2b48c6d5c4e254349ce9675b850d2da89b42bdf3b62cf5b1c84`.

Exact writable files:

- `crates/hyperai-local-service/src/storage.rs`: add context only to the
  test's `initialize_home` and `backup_metadata` error propagation; do not
  change production storage code or restore behavior.
- `docs/compute-bazaar-storage-homebusy-diagnostic-packet.md`: record the
  diagnostic command and exact result.
- `docs/state-slices.md`: this authorization and result.
- `docs/compute-bazaar-rust-port-subplan.md`: concise root-validation status.

Allowed effects: run
`CARGO_NET_OFFLINE=true sh scripts/with-pinned-rust.sh cargo test -p hyperai-local-service --lib -- --nocapture`
once. This may execute the crate's local synthetic unit fixtures and their
test-owned child process, but it must not contact a provider, registry,
pre-existing service, external host, browser, or chain. Also run pinned Rust
format checking, root `lint:fast`, import verification, and `git diff --check`.
Do not run root `verify:full` or any nested upstream workspace. If this
bounded package test fails with the same error, stop and research the lock,
fixture, and test-isolation causes before another test attempt.

Non-goals: changing production lock behavior, retrying the full workspace
suite, altering storage semantics, touching user data or a persistent HyperAI
home, enabling networking, or claiming root lint completion.

Proof gates: test-only context identifies whether initialization or backup
returns the error; the bounded package unit target records a complete
pass/fail result; pinned format, root fast lint, import preservation, and diff
hygiene pass; all unrelated working-tree paths remain untouched.

Claim ceiling: this one local test path only. Reviewer status is
`NOT_REQUESTED`; reproduction is `NOT_REPRODUCED`. Root `verify:full` remains
unverified until the earlier failure has a supported cause and the broader
gate completes.

Publish boundary: local source and documentation only; no commit, PR, release,
publication, service launch, or external effect.

Implementation/evidence (2026-10-01): test-only error context was added to
the `initialize_home` and `backup_metadata` calls. The exact bounded offline
`hyperai-local-service --lib` run passed 11/11 under default parallel
libtest; neither labeled call failed. This does not explain the prior root
`HomeBusy`. Root `lint:fast` passed 21 interface tests, 3 installer tests,
pinned formatting, and strict Clippy. Import verification passed all three
recorded trees and `git diff --check` passed. Exact command, toolchain,
source digest, custody, and claim ceiling are in the
[diagnostic packet](compute-bazaar-storage-homebusy-diagnostic-packet.md).
Assurance is `INTERNAL_PASS` for this local-service unit-test set, but the
prior root failure diagnosis remains `INCONCLUSIVE`. Do not rerun root
`verify:full` from this slice.

## `hyperai.bazaar_interface.mobile_nav_keyboard.v1`

Status: implemented and locally browser-tested under the user-directed
HyperAI interface work. It changes keyboard focus and closed-state exposure for
the existing mobile navigation disclosure; it adds no data, service, or
connector behavior.

Purpose: while the mobile navigation is closed, keep its off-canvas controls
out of the accessibility tree and keyboard order. When it opens, expose its
disclosure state and move focus to the current navigation control; allow
ordinary Tab navigation through the drawer and restore focus to the toggle
when Escape closes it. Selecting a destination continues to focus the
destination page.

Exact files:

- `apps/hyperai-interface/index.html`: associate the toggle with the sidebar.
- `apps/hyperai-interface/app.js`: set focus on open while retaining the
  existing Escape and route-selection focus behavior.
- `apps/hyperai-interface/app.css`: only if needed to preserve visible focus
  and responsive navigation behavior.
- `docs/compute-bazaar-phase-2-data-packet.md`: record the scoped browser
  qualification and remaining accessibility limitations.
- `docs/state-slices.md`: this authorization and evidence record.

Allowed effects: local browser DOM and keyboard focus changes for the mobile
navigation disclosure; browser qualification against a disposable HyperAI
synthetic home served on IPv4 loopback; and edits to the exact files above.
This does not start or connect an external service.

Non-goals: changing desktop navigation order, adding modal focus trapping,
changing page or API behavior, persisting navigation state, changing market
or Data contracts, or connecting any source, agent, provider, fleet, wallet,
chain, or reviewer.

Claim ceiling: keyboard focus and disclosure behavior in the local browser
workspace on the tested host and viewport. This does not establish
screen-reader acceptance, cross-browser support, or general accessibility.

Proof gates: at a mobile viewport, confirm closed navigation controls are
inert and hidden from the accessibility tree; from keyboard input, open the
navigation and verify focus enters the current navigation control; Tab reaches
subsequent navigation controls; activating a destination closes the disclosure
and focuses the page; Escape closes it and restores focus to the toggle;
`aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` match the rendered state; visible focus
remains present; and the tested viewport range has no document-level
horizontal overflow. At desktop widths, confirm the sidebar is exposed and
usable. Verify JavaScript syntax and record browser errors and the remaining
screen-reader, cross-browser, broader reduced-motion, and clean-reproduction
gates.

Implementation evidence: the mobile toggle now declares `aria-controls`; the
closed off-canvas sidebar is `inert` and `aria-hidden`; opening it exposes the
sidebar and focuses the current page's navigation button. Escape closes the
disclosure and returns focus to the toggle. Route selection closes the drawer
and focuses the selected page.

Browser evidence (2026-09-25): on macOS 26.6.1 arm64, using the pinned Rust
1.93.1 service on `127.0.0.1:4318` and a disposable HyperAI synthetic home,
keyboard Tab skipped the closed drawer and reached the mobile toggle. Enter
opened the drawer, focused the active page control, and subsequent Tab keys
reached other destinations. Enter selected Data and Fleet; each route closed
the drawer, hid/inerted it, and focused the page. Escape restored focus to the
toggle. The AX tree omitted closed navigation; `aria-expanded`,
`aria-controls`, and `aria-hidden` matched each state. The focused toggle had a
visible 3 px outline. On the Data page, keyboard navigation and Enter ran the
bounded query and moved focus to its status message reporting 3 rows across 3
columns from the synthetic JSON snapshot.

At 320, 390, and 768 px, the mobile toggle was visible and the closed drawer
was inert/hidden; at 1024 and 1440 px, the sidebar was exposed and the mobile
toggle hidden. Document and body widths matched the viewport at all five
widths. Browser console errors were empty. Rust `lint:fast` and JavaScript
syntax checks passed. Asset SHA-256: `index.html`
`47ec49fb128acc8a4601c3554ea4f53e630f054132be0471dfff58109c9a9fe0`;
`app.js` `f4daa61b1db3485f35db1633d6a725f20b2681737f05e1e50f98378e43a54f50`;
`app.css`
`52a34558e3e1aa6eac20fd52a4c61ddd1163e8c9a30efd642cc2189bef6ffcf1`.

Assurance remains `NOT_ASSIGNED`; reviewer status is `NOT_REQUESTED`;
reproduction status is `NOT_REPRODUCED`. The temporary home and browser tab
were removed/closed, port 4318 was stopped, and the pre-existing service on
port 4317 was preserved. Screen-reader use, cross-browser behavior, and the
full interface keyboard path remain untested.

Reduced-motion browser qualification (2026-09-26): on macOS 26.6.1 arm64 with
Brave 154.1.96.59, Node 22.23.2, and `puppeteer-core` 25.3.0, the current
workspace shell was served by `target/debug/hyperai` on `127.0.0.1:4318` from
a disposable synthetic home. The binary SHA-256 was
`154b4df154cb841fd898d4650d49434a9ab72431a70caa140f7d087ff26cabe4`. Served
`index.html`, `app.js`, and `app.css` matched the workspace byte-for-byte at
SHA-256 `8f15d9272533e8672e7d91ff1c00d364a82257175549cf787c7e858e7b1230b7`,
`750416e0fbe1adb878268c45174b4a3571ca43680ffe6969003c1e3b29ae9d5b`, and
`52a34558e3e1aa6eac20fd52a4c61ddd1163e8c9a30efd642cc2189bef6ffcf1`,
respectively. At 375×812, browser-emulated `no-preference` produced a `0.2s`
sidebar transition; emulated `reduce` matched the media query and computed
`1e-05s`. The AX tree exposed the closed control as a button named “Open
navigation”. Opening set `aria-expanded=true`, exposed the sidebar, moved focus
to Overview, and placed the sidebar at x=0. Escape closed it, restored focus to
the toggle, set the sidebar inert and hidden, and moved it offscreen. The
browser allowed requests only to the loopback service; no other requests were
attempted and no page errors occurred. The service stopped, its temporary home
was removed, and the pre-existing listener on port 4317 remained unchanged.

This is bounded reduced-motion and accessibility-tree evidence for the mobile
navigation in one browser and viewport. Assurance remains `NOT_ASSIGNED`;
reviewer status is `NOT_REQUESTED`; reproduction is `NOT_REPRODUCED`. It does
not establish VoiceOver/screen-reader operation, reduced-motion behavior across
all workspaces, cross-browser behavior, or general accessibility acceptance.

## `hyperai.bazaar_interface.workspace_keyboard_routes.v1`

Status: locally browser-checked; no code changed and no external authority is
granted.

Purpose: qualify keyboard activation of the HyperAI interface's top-level
workspace destinations on the desktop browser layout. This records route
navigation and focus transfer only; it is not a full keyboard or accessibility
acceptance result.

Exact files:

- `docs/bazaar-hyperai-interface-plan.md`: record the interface follow-up and
  its claim limit.
- `docs/state-slices.md`: this scope and its browser evidence.

Allowed effects: navigate the local browser among the existing workspaces and
issue their ordinary same-origin read requests against a disposable synthetic
home; record the result in these documentation files. No application data,
provider, seller, external agent, or network service is used.

Non-goals: changing interface behavior, running action controls, proving
screen-reader or full keyboard-only operation, testing reduced motion,
qualifying mobile/tablet layouts, or authorizing a source connection or
external operation.

Claim ceiling: on the tested macOS browser at a 1280 px desktop viewport, Enter
activates each of the 11 top-level workspaces, the expected workspace heading
renders, focus moves to `#page-root`, the document does not overflow
horizontally, and no browser console errors are reported. This does not prove
all controls are keyboard-operable or accessible.

Browser evidence (2026-09-25): baseline HyperAI revision
`dcf41e31aa1f98438a6f8ec6cb253801e26dc0aa`, with the local dirty working tree;
macOS 26.6.1 arm64; Rust `1.93.1`; `target/debug/hyperai-ui` SHA-256
`387c0c91e2550c25a794619e736d21d175d390a5ab5cb60b57291c424ed29ef6`;
`Cargo.lock` SHA-256
`8b010b3251babf567b4c8ad8636ae01d4cdc9b58155fe61013542b71f865dfda`;
browser assets match the digests recorded under
`hyperai.bazaar_interface.mobile_nav_keyboard.v1`. On a disposable local
synthetic home, Enter activated Overview, Market, Deals, Data, Inference,
Fleet, Eval, Evidence, Agents & Access, Activity, and Trade. Each route showed
its matching breadcrumb and heading and focused the workspace root; all 11
reported `document.scrollWidth <= window.innerWidth`. Browser console errors
were empty. Only same-origin local UI requests were made; no form or write
action was invoked.

Assurance level: `NOT_ASSIGNED`. Reviewer status: `NOT_REQUESTED`.
Reproducibility status: `NOT_REPRODUCED`; no clean second environment was
used. Data and artifact custody: fixed HyperAI synthetic records stayed in a
disposable local home and the browser session; no result or input artifact was
persisted or exported.

Known limitations: this check covers desktop top-level route activation only.
Full in-page keyboard operation, screen-reader behavior, reduced-motion
emulation, cross-browser behavior, and narrow/tablet layouts remain open.
Next gate: complete those local accessibility checks; external integrations
still require their own rights decisions and exact state slices.

## `hyperai.bazaar_rust_port_current_host_validation.v1`

Status: documentation-only record of a current-host, offline validation sweep
across the implemented Rust compute-desk packages. The sweep changed no source

## `hyperai.bazaar_rust_port_dependency_yank_review.v1`

Status: accepted narrow lockfile-maintenance continuation under the user's
direction to follow the Rust compute-desk subplan. This slice updates only the
two yanked transitive package resolutions recorded by the Phase 1 packet.

Purpose: resolve `chacha20 0.10.1` to the compatible non-yanked `0.10.2` and
`spin 0.9.8` to the compatible non-yanked `0.9.9` in the root lockfile. The
workspace manifests, APIs, feature selections, and source files remain fixed.

Exact files: root `Cargo.lock`; this state-slice record; and the Phase 1 packet
and Rust compute-desk subplan entries that report the dependency-review result.

Allowed effects: targeted offline Cargo lock resolution for exactly those two
packages; focused offline tests for the affected local workspace paths; and
documentation of checksums, package-resolution evidence, and test results.
Keep all pre-existing lockfile entries and unrelated dirty work unchanged.

Non-goals: changing any manifest, feature, toolchain, source file, package
script, upstream repository, product workspace, fixture, or data; broad Cargo
updates; fetching new packages; provider or network calls; release or
publication; and external execution or settlement.

Claim ceiling: the root lockfile resolves these two packages to the recorded
non-yanked versions, and the named focused local checks pass on this host.
This is dependency-resolution and local compatibility evidence only; it is
not a security audit, independent review, clean-environment reproduction, or
release authorization.

Proof gates: confirm registry-index yank flags, checksums, Rust-version
requirements, and semver constraints from cached package metadata and
authoritative upstream records; use only targeted `cargo update --offline
-p <package> --precise <version>` operations; compare the full lockfile package
map before and after to ensure only the two selected versions changed; run
focused locked/offline checks; and retain explicit failure or inconclusive
results. No publish or release action is included.

Resolution evidence (2026-09-26, macOS 26.6.1 arm64, pinned Rust/Cargo
1.93.1): the saved pre-change lockfile has SHA-256
`289596de2cddd9cd5deab92260961cf084c8f44a241f7e27fee4810375cafcbd`; the
resulting lockfile has SHA-256
`7da69749f4bdd789e2512cec4d3f2522cddec1944b6ff7e35584b7f9ee343461`. Both
lockfiles contain 543 registry/workspace package records; the package-map
comparison found no additions or removals and exactly the two version and
checksum changes below:

| Package | Previous lock entry | Current lock entry | Cached index rust-version |
|---|---|---|---|
| `chacha20` | `0.10.1`, yanked, checksum `d524456ba66e72eb8b115ff89e01e497f8e6d11d78b70b1aa13c0fbd97540a81` | `0.10.2`, not yanked in the inspected index, checksum `65c35e4b699c7e15ccbe7ee35c005e4fc0a278d22238a2857e6ce2dadeda1b06` | `1.85` for both versions |
| `spin` | `0.9.8`, yanked, checksum `6980e8d7511241f8acf4aebddbb1ff938df5eebe98691418c4468d0b72a96a67` | `0.9.9`, not yanked in the inspected index, checksum `3763264f6b73151db08c50ff20d7d8a0b8796e021cdea7ceedad07b80155fa0e` | `1.38` for both versions |

The cached `.crate` archives for all four versions hash to their respective
cached registry-index checksums. The cached `rand 0.10.2` metadata requires
`chacha20 ^0.10.0`; `flume 0.11.1` uses the `spin` package through the `spin1`
alias with requirement `^0.9.8`. Both selected versions satisfy those ranges.
The inspected metadata is a local registry-index snapshot, not a continuing
guarantee that a registry will retain the same yank flags. Cargo's resolver
documentation explains that yanked versions are ignored for new resolution
unless already locked or explicitly selected. The upstream [ChaCha20
changelog](https://github.com/RustCrypto/stream-ciphers/blob/master/chacha20/CHANGELOG.md)
marks `0.10.1` yanked and records the SSE4.1-in-SSE2-backend fix in `0.10.2`.
The [spin changelog](https://github.com/zesterer/spin-rs/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md)
records a `Once::try_call_once` fix in `0.9.8`; this record does not infer why
that release is yanked or attribute that reason to a later release. See the
[Cargo dependency-resolution documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/resolver.html#yanked-versions).

The exact focused command
`sh scripts/with-pinned-rust.sh cargo test --locked --offline --jobs 2 --all-targets -p outcomes-persistence-sqlx -p hyperai-local-service -p outcomes-cli`
passed: 81 passed, 0 failed, 2 ignored. The ignored tests are the PostgreSQL

range evidence, and no network retry was made.

## `hyperai.bazaar.acp_packet.v1`

Status: documentation-only Phase 8 ACP packet. It defines the proposed local
synthetic implementation contract and agent trust boundary; it authorizes no
code change, ACP-agent launch, model/provider call, or data disclosure.

Purpose: scope ACP protocol negotiation, session lifecycle, typed read-only
tools, profile/process boundary, shared-client integration, and qualification
gates before a separate implementation slice is accepted.

Included files:

- `docs/compute-bazaar-phase-8-acp-packet.md`: protocol/dependency choices,
  profile and tool contract, exact implementation file map, limits, and proof
  gates.
- `docs/compute-bazaar-rust-port-subplan.md`: link and status for Phase 8.
- `docs/state-slices.md`: this documentation-only authorization record.

Allowed effects: inspect the current HyperAI plans, ACP dependency metadata,
and official ACP v1 and Rust SDK documentation; edit only these three
Markdown files.

Non-goals: changing Rust, JavaScript, HTML, CSS, manifests, lockfiles, package
scripts, products, fixtures, or ignored Bazaar files; adding or resolving a
dependency; launching any ACP peer; contacting agents, models, providers,
registries, fleets, reviewers, wallets, or chains; processing real-user data;
publishing; or authorizing the proposed `hyperai.bazaar.acp.v1` code slice.

Claim ceiling: planning only. The SDK version and local contract choices are
not runtime, sandbox, agent, provider, external-review, or production
evidence.

Proof gates: verify the SDK crate metadata and protocol boundary against
official sources; state the inherited-process trust limitation; preserve the
stable-v1-only decision and no-provider boundary; review file links and
`git diff --check`; assign no runtime assurance level.

## `hyperai.bazaar.acp.v1`

Status: accepted under the user's direction to follow the Rust compute-desk
subplan. Implementation is local-only; qualification uses a HyperAI-authored
synthetic peer and fixed synthetic data. This does not authorize connecting a
third-party agent, contacting a model/provider, or disclosing real-user data.

Purpose: add the stable-v1 ACP client/session surface and a fixed read-only
tool bridge through the existing HyperAI application facade, local service,
CLI, TUI, and browser shell.

Exact files: `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`; new
`crates/hyperai-acp/Cargo.toml`, `src/lib.rs`, `src/profile.rs`,
`src/session.rs`, `src/tools.rs`, `src/bin/acp-fixture-peer.rs`, and
`tests/synthetic_peer.rs`; new `crates/hyperai-mcp/Cargo.toml`, `src/lib.rs`,
`src/main.rs`, and named tests; `crates/hyperai-application/Cargo.toml` and
`src/lib.rs`; `crates/hyperai-local-service/Cargo.toml`, `src/auth.rs`,
`src/server.rs`, and `tests/agent_api.rs`; `crates/outcomes-cli/Cargo.toml`
and `src/lib.rs`; `crates/hyperai-tui/Cargo.toml`, `src/lib.rs`, and
`tests/terminal_restore.rs`; `crates/outcomes-cli/tests/cli_compat.rs`;
`apps/hyperai-interface/index.html`, `app.js`, and `app.css`; `README.md`;
the Phase 8 packet, Rust port subplan, and this record. No additional path is
implied by imports.

Allowed effects: local IPv4-loopback session lifecycle; explicit user-started
profiles; ACP v1 only; bounded, read-only Data/Fleet/Eval/Trade operations over
the already authorized synthetic fixtures through standard MCP stdio; volatile
session state; aggregate ACP stdout up to 8 MiB and stderr up to 64 KiB per
session; and the packet's synthetic-peer tests. The already listed TUI client
may preserve the local service's stable error status, code, and message for
interactive diagnostics, with bounded control-character-free text; this does
not change the service response contract or expose request bodies. The
already listed MCP bridge may forward only HTTP status and a validated error
code from the `hyperai.interface.error.v1` response through ACP's generic
internal-error data; it must omit the service message and response body, and
malformed or unknown envelopes must map to `UNKNOWN_ERROR`. This is diagnostic
only and does not change tool permissions. Use
`agent-client-protocol = 2.2.0`, `agent-client-protocol-rmcp = 3.1.1` with
default features disabled, the pinned Rust toolchain, and locked dependencies.
Keep `unstable_protocol_v2` and `unstable_mcp_over_acp` disabled. Any local
process used in a test is a HyperAI-authored fixture with a temporary home and
no network access.

Platform scope: the current child-process lifecycle uses Unix process groups.
Windows process ownership is implemented behind the optional default-off
`windows-acp` feature using Job Objects. Locked MSVC all-target checks and
strict Clippy pass with the feature both disabled and enabled, but no Windows
binary has been executed. Windows support remains unclaimed until native
connect/disconnect, failed-handshake, cancellation, parent/descendant cleanup,
and supervisor-abort tests pass. Windows core-desk support does not enable ACP
for Windows. Other unsupported targets and Windows builds without the feature
return `UnsupportedPlatform` before launching the profile. See
[`hyperai.bazaar.acp_windows_process_ownership.v1`](#hyperai-bazaar-acp_windows_process_ownershipv1).

Non-goals: starting a third-party or remotely hosted agent during this work;
model/provider calls; sending prompts or real records to external systems;
filesystem or terminal capabilities; arbitrary shell/process tools; quote
approval/completion; market fulfillment; live or state-changing Fleet work;
Eval runs or score-based promotion; financial Trade; outcome resolution;
JustAI or ESN projections; provider calls; external publication; testnet
writes; or production deployment.

Process boundary: HyperAI-mediated tools are read-only. ACP does not sandbox a
selected agent executable or restrict tools, filesystem, network, or
credentials available to that process outside HyperAI. Do not claim that the
profile itself is sandboxed or read-only. A later real-agent connection and
any model/provider data disclosure require a separate exact user authorization
and an appropriate process-isolation and data-disclosure review.

Claim ceiling: local ACP v1 negotiation, session/event handling, cancellation,
and synthetic read-only MCP tool calls exercised through the packaged HyperAI
MCP stdio sidecar and HyperAI-authored peer using a service-issued capability.
No third-party-client compatibility, real-agent compatibility or safety,
provider behavior, sandbox, independent review, or production claim.

Proof gates: satisfy every acceptance gate in the Phase 8 packet; confirm the
protocol-v2 and native MCP-over-ACP Cargo features are absent; verify that tools call only the shared
facade and enforce their fixed allowlist; cover malformed/batched input,
limits, cancellation, disconnect, and uncertain process exit; confirm prompts,
tool payloads, credentials, and traces are not persisted or logged; distinguish
the bounded volatile assistant-text display buffer from durable metadata; run
focused checks and root `corepack pnpm run lint`; report root and nested
workspace validation separately. The TUI error adapter must retain the
service's stable status/code/message on synthetic and isolated local-service
error responses and bound display text without admitting control characters.
The MCP bridge must retain
only bounded HTTP status and a validated error code for the stable error
schema; malformed, oversized, and unknown envelopes must stay generic, with
no request or response payload forwarded. No real agent or provider is
contacted.

Linux/amd64 process-cleanup diagnosis (2026-09-25): an offline run of the
synthetic peer integration test first failed because the test used
`kill(pid, 0)` as a liveness check. `/proc/<pid>/stat` showed the descendant in
state `Z`, with PPID 1 and PGRP equal to the ACP peer PID: the process group had
been terminated, while the no-init container's PID 1 had not reaped the
orphaned zombie. The same test passed with Docker `--init`. The regression test
now treats Linux `Z` and `X` states as exited while still failing for a live
process. After that change, the nine-test `hyperai-acp` synthetic-peer suite
passed in the Linux/amd64 Debian container without `--init` and on macOS arm64;
the process-group test also passed three repeated no-init runs and a run with

Rust/Cargo 1.93.1, disabled networking, read-only source and Cargo-registry

Purpose: add a HyperAI-owned, source-labelled local catalog and a bounded,
read-only JSON/Parquet query path through the existing application facade,
service, CLI, TUI, and browser interface. It remains separate from the
caller-pinned Simple Compute Market capture explorer already in the Data
workspace.

Baseline: HyperAI `dcf41e31aa1f98438a6f8ec6cb253801e26dc0aa` on `main`, plus
the existing uncommitted monorepo and Phase 1 work. Preserve all unrelated
dirty and untracked paths.

Included files:

- `Cargo.toml` and `Cargo.lock`: register and lock the independently owned
  `hyperai-data` crate and the selected local query-engine dependencies.
- `crates/hyperai-data/Cargo.toml`, `src/lib.rs`,
  `tests/catalog_contract.rs`, and `tests/query_contract.rs`: versioned local
  dataset manifests/catalog, deterministic synthetic records, path and digest
  verification, read-only query planning/execution, result limits, and stable
  JSON/CSV output.
- `crates/hyperai-application/Cargo.toml` and `src/lib.rs`: compose typed Data
  operations without taking ownership of source rights, market eligibility,
  outcomes, custody, or provider execution.
- `crates/hyperai-local-service/Cargo.toml`, `src/server.rs`, and
  `tests/data_api.rs`: authenticated local catalog/query/model/view routes
  using the current API error, body, timeout, and session contracts.
- `crates/outcomes-cli/src/lib.rs` and `crates/outcomes-cli/tests/cli_compat.rs`:
  read-only `hyperai data` commands and explicit local saved-model/view
  creation under the selected HyperAI home; loopback readiness checks tolerate
  a cold start of the expanded monorepo CLI and bypass ambient proxies.
- `crates/hyperai-tui/src/lib.rs`: connect the Data workspace to the shared
  typed service results; no query policy or data access outside the service.
- `apps/hyperai-interface/app.js` and `app.css`: present owned local datasets,
  provenance, query controls/results, saved definitions, and limits separately
  from caller-verified SCM captures; do not alter unrelated navigation or
  workflows.
- `README.md`, `docs/state-slices.md`,
  `docs/compute-bazaar-phase-2-data-packet.md`,
  `docs/compute-bazaar-rust-port-subplan.md`, and
  `docs/bazaar-hyperai-interface-plan.md`: document the feature and record
  only evidence actually produced.

Allowed effects: deterministic synthetic records created in temporary test
homes; read-only scans of the HyperAI-owned local data root; local persistence
of explicit user-created query-model and view definitions; bounded query work
and results; local service API reads; and validation commands listed in the
packet. Inputs and outputs stay local. The Rust toolchain remains pinned at
1.93.1 and dependencies remain locked.

Hard limits: accept no provider, registry, Bazaar, HyperIntel, JustAI, SCM,
network, cloud, database-service, or caller-selected external path inputs. Do
not read arbitrary host paths, follow symlinks, auto-ingest files, or copy
SCM capture bytes into this catalog. Do not load real-user or restricted data
in this slice. Do not enable DDL, DML, file/network table functions, extension
loading, recursive SQL, unbounded scans, spill files, or background jobs.
Queries may see only tables registered from a verified manifest beneath the
HyperAI data root. Local model/view files contain query definitions and
digests only, not input or result payloads.

Non-goals: Bazaar code/schema/query/data/fixture/model/view/benchmark/asset
reuse; source import or feed connection; medallion ingestion/transforms;
provider/fleet operations; offers, deals, settlement, outcome resolution,
inference execution, JustAI projection, external publication, cross-device
sync, and production deployment.

Claim ceiling: locally created deterministic synthetic records can be listed
and queried by this HyperAI build under the stated limits. Manifest digests
establish byte identity only. Query success, price fields, and sample
availability do not establish source truth, freshness, seller identity,
resource capacity, correct computation, buyer approval, or payment
entitlement.

Proof gates: manifest rebuild is byte-deterministic; altered bytes, schema
drift, path traversal, symlink escape, unknown tables/functions, DDL/DML,
recursive SQL, multiple statements, and malformed SQL fail closed; query
cancellation and wall-time/input-byte/row/output-byte/memory limits are
exercised; JSON and CSV output is deterministic for a fixed synthetic
release; stale and absent data remain explicit; explicit model/view writes
stay beneath the home; API auth and stable errors hold; CLI/TUI/browser clients
all use the same facade; no network or Bazaar read occurs; and root diff
hygiene passes. Measure a fixed memory baseline under representative scans;
do not report a bounded-memory claim until measured against its named host and
dataset.

snapshot and cancellation behavior below. Overall Phase 2 Data acceptance

Purpose: make one DataFusion query consume exactly the bounded byte snapshot
whose manifest length and SHA-256 were verified. The previous path-based scan
reopened the dataset after pre-scan hashing; this slice closes that gap by
registering the verified capture in a private per-query memory object store.

  `object_store` memory implementation with default features disabled; do not
  enable cloud or HTTP backends.

  `tests/query_contract.rs`: bounded capture, length/digest verification, and
  query registration from one per-query in-memory snapshot.
- `crates/hyperai-local-service/src/server.rs` and
  `tests/data_api.rs`: a test-only gate between active-query registration and
  execution, so the authenticated HTTP cancellation route is exercised without
  depending on query duration. The gate must be absent from non-test builds and
  must not add an API route or production delay.
- `docs/compute-bazaar-phase-2-data-packet.md`,
  `docs/compute-bazaar-rust-port-subplan.md`, and this state-slice record.

Allowed effects: read only the existing deterministic synthetic JSON/Parquet
files beneath the HyperAI data root; hold up to the existing 16 MiB input cap
in process memory for one query; register that immutable buffer in a private
in-memory object store for the DataFusion session; and run the existing
read-only query with unchanged limits and result schemas. A `cfg(test)`-only
service gate may pause the query after active registration while the existing
authenticated cancel route is exercised, then release it to confirm a
cancelled error with no partial result. All snapshots and object stores are
dropped when the query returns or is cancelled. No durable write, temp file,
network request, provider call, or non-synthetic input is allowed.

Storage recovery contract refinement (2026-09-28): the accepted packet now
defines offline `hyperai storage backup` and `hyperai storage restore
--backup-name NAME` commands for the local schema-v1 `desk_meta` table only.
Backup creates a consistent, no-overwrite snapshot and reports its basename
and SHA-256. Restore requires the service lock and initialization lock,
validates a same-home generated backup, creates a pre-restore safety snapshot,
and replaces metadata rows transactionally. No HTTP route is added. The
existing migration backup is not treated as a user-restorable v1 backup.
Implementation is present in the local-service storage module, its storage
tests, the shared CLI, and the CLI compatibility tests. It has no service
route and does not move records from another product.

Windows MSVC target cross-check (2026-09-28): pinned Rust `1.93.1` with
`x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` installed on macOS `26.6.1` arm64. A Windows-target
check of the service, TUI, and CLI package graph stopped in `zstd-sys`: Apple
Clang lacked the Windows C runtime/SDK headers `stdlib.h` and `string.h`.

dependency because Trade depends on `hyperai-data`/DataFusion. The initial
offline invocation also reported the locked Windows-only `crossterm_winapi`
crate was not cached; the subsequent `--locked` invocation downloaded the
locked crate set without changing project dependency declarations.

After following that dependency path, the narrower command
`sh scripts/with-pinned-rust.sh cargo check --locked --offline --jobs 1
--all-targets --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc -p hyperai-foundation
-p hyperai-market -p hyperai-fleet -p hyperai-eval` passed. This type-checks
those four Rust-only crates and their test targets; it does not link Windows
binaries or exercise service, storage, ACL, terminal, or process behavior.
Assurance is `INTERNAL_PASS` for that exact cross-target type-check only;
reviewer status is `NOT_REQUESTED`, and reproducibility is `NOT_REPRODUCED`.
No Windows runtime or user data was used, and no workspace source or lockfile
was changed by the cross-check. Windows remains unqualified until the declared
MSVC service lifecycle, ACL, auth/path, and TUI matrix runs on a Windows host.
Rust's target documentation says non-Windows MSVC cross-compilation may be
possible but is unsupported; Microsoft's Windows SDK provides the required
headers and libraries. `cargo-xwin` is a possible SDK/CRT cross-check route,
but its documented use carries a Microsoft SDK license condition; that route
was not used. See the [Rust MSVC target documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/rustc/platform-support/windows-msvc.html),
[Microsoft SDK requirements](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/learnwin32/prepare-your-development-environment),
and [cargo-xwin README](https://github.com/rust-cross/cargo-xwin).

## `hyperai.bazaar_interface.shell.v1`

Status: implemented locally. Focused Rust compilation and Clippy, JavaScript
syntax, loopback API, and desktop browser checks passed. A 390 px browser pass
also verified mobile navigation labels after route selection, Escape-to-close
with focus restoration, and no document-level horizontal overflow on the
Activity, Market, and Data paths. Full interface acceptance and broader
Bazaar-inspired integrations remain open. This does not connect any external
product runtime.

Purpose: establish the HyperAI navigation, connection-status model, provenance
and claim labels, and a user-visible synthetic Market-to-Deal-to-Evidence
vertical path using the existing Rust market contract.

Included files:

- `apps/hyperai-interface/index.html`, `app.css`, and `app.js`: independently
  authored, dependency-free local interface assets. No Bazaar source, design
  assets, data, fixtures, schemas, or generated output are reused.
- `crates/hyperai-application/`: typed read-only connection inventory and
  facade functions over the existing local synthetic market contracts.
- `crates/outcomes-cli/src/bin/hyperai-ui.rs`: loopback-only HTTP host for the
  static interface and versioned local API. It exposes status, synthetic demo,
  and offline receipt verification routes only.
- `crates/outcomes-cli/Cargo.toml`, root `Cargo.toml`, and `Cargo.lock`:
  register the facade and UI host within the existing Rust workspace.
- `package.json`: one local launch command for the interface.
- `README.md`, `docs/bazaar-hyperai-interface-plan.md`, and this record:
  document the working slice, commands, limits, and later gates.

Allowed effects: serve the bundled HyperAI-authored assets on IPv4 loopback;
return a static connection inventory; create the existing deterministic
synthetic receipt in memory; and verify a caller-provided local receipt body
under the existing market contract. No artifact is persisted by the interface.

Non-goals: connecting to or copying from the Compute Bazaar reference; calling
Simple Compute Market, HyperIntel, JustAI, ESN-JustNet, Composed Platform,
providers, sellers, agents, fleets, wallets, or chains; performing paid
execution, live negotiation, SSH, external evidence publication, settlement,
Trade, or production deployment; and claiming that all planned product
surfaces are integrated.

Claim ceiling: local interface and API behavior over the existing deterministic
synthetic Rust market contract, with local structural and signature consistency
checks only. Connection inventory entries are explicit workspace/reference
status descriptions, not health checks. No seller identity, hardware, correct
computation, market freshness, payment, external reviewer, or production claim.

Stop conditions: bind only to `127.0.0.1`; do not add configurable non-loopback
binding or cross-origin access; reject malformed or oversized verification
requests; keep all upstream connectors inactive; preserve Bazaar as ignored
reference-only material; and preserve unrelated dirty files and product
workspaces.

Completed checks: `cargo check -p hyperai-application -p outcomes-cli
--all-targets`; strict Clippy for those targets; root Rust formatting check;
`node --check` for the interface script; loopback HTTP smoke checks for static
assets, CSP headers, status inventory, synthetic demo, offline receipt
verification, and malformed receipt rejection; and browser interaction through
Overview, Market, Deals, Evidence, and Agents & access. The receipt digest
matched across the demo and verification responses. On mobile, selecting a
navigation item now closes the menu with `aria-expanded="false"` and the
accessible name `Open navigation`; Escape also closes it and restores focus to
the toggle. These are local checks, not an independent review or production
gate.

Remaining gates: complete screen-reader, keyboard-only navigation across all
controls, broader reduced-motion coverage (mobile navigation has one bounded
browser check; see `hyperai.bazaar_interface.mobile_nav_keyboard.v1`), and
responsive acceptance; run the root
repository gate when preparing a broader integration change; and create

## `hyperai.bazaar_interface.synthetic_quote_review.v1`

Status: implemented in the working tree. Rust compilation, strict Clippy,
formatting, JavaScript syntax, and desktop browser smoke checks passed. The
loopback API smoke exercised preview, approval, mock completion, receipt
verification, and changed-digest rejection. Narrow-screen, broader
accessibility, and automated contract checks remain open; this slice has no
`INTERNAL_PASS` claim.

Baseline revision: `dcf41e31aa1f98438a6f8ec6cb253801e26dc0aa` on `main`;
implementation and this proof record are working-tree edits.

Purpose: advance the Deals surface from an all-at-once mock lifecycle to a
staged quote review. Render the exact synthetic buyer request and seller quote
before a separate user action asks the market contract to create a synthetic
buyer-approved deal. The preview digest binds the entire displayed fixture;
the approval request carries only that digest and the market module rebuilds
and checks the preview before signing.

Included files:

- `crates/hyperai-market/src/lib.rs`: source-owned deterministic quote
  preview and digest-checked synthetic approval contract, reusing the
  existing synthetic catalog and signing keys.
- `crates/hyperai-application/src/lib.rs`: typed preview and approval facade.
- `crates/outcomes-cli/src/bin/hyperai-ui.rs`: loopback-only preview and
  approval API routes; no additional network or persistence behavior.
- `apps/hyperai-interface/app.js` and `app.css`: staged deal review, explicit
  approval action, accessible progress/error messaging, and synthetic-key
  disclosure.
- `README.md`: local interface launch and staged-flow behavior.
- `docs/bazaar-hyperai-interface-plan.md` and `docs/state-slices.md`: phase
  progress, boundaries, proof status, and remaining gates.

Allowed effects: build and return deterministic synthetic market records in
memory; recompute the exact preview when its digest is submitted; and create a
synthetic buyer signature bound to the approved quote using the existing
fixture key. Use only the contract's simulated fixture timestamps. No file,
network, seller, provider, agent, fleet, wallet, chain, or public evidence
effect is permitted.

Non-goals: live registry reads, seller storefront negotiation, real buyer
identity or signer custody, dynamic price or availability data, job
specification or private input handling, fulfillment, metering, verification,
settlement, payment, persistent deals, or production UX authorization.

Claim ceiling: a local UI can display an exact, digest-bound synthetic quote
and exercise the existing buyer-approval contract with a deterministic test
key. It does not establish user identity, a real user signature, seller
identity, quote freshness, available capacity, correct computation, payment,
independent verification, or production readiness.

Proof gates: keep the quote and buyer request under the market module's
existing validators; bind the complete preview to the digest; reject changed
or unknown preview digests; ensure no approval is created before the explicit
action; label the fixture clock and buyer key as synthetic; preserve the
loopback-only host and existing CSP; and keep all inputs and results in
memory. Focused `cargo check -p hyperai-market -p hyperai-application
-p outcomes-cli --all-targets`, strict Clippy for the same packages,
`rustfmt --check` for changed Rust files, and `node --check` for the interface
script pass. A loopback API smoke passed preview, approval, mock completion,
receipt verification, and mismatched-preview/deal rejection (`409`). A
desktop browser smoke exercised preview and explicit synthetic approval.
Narrow-screen review, adversarial review, and automated contract checks remain
unrun.

Assurance level: no named assurance level assigned; `INTERNAL_PASS` criteria
are not met by compilation, static checks, and a bounded API smoke alone.
Reviewer status:
`NOT_REQUESTED`. Reproducibility status: `NOT_REPRODUCED`; no clean second
environment was used. Only deterministic synthetic records and the existing
fixture key bytes are referenced; no real user data, provider payload, or
external artifact was introduced or persisted. The changed-input rejection
path returned the expected local contract errors in the API smoke.

Known limitations: the displayed clock and approval time are fixed simulation
times, so quote expiry is not wall-clock freshness; the approval is signed by
the deterministic fixture key, not a person; the in-memory result is not a
persistent deal; and narrow-screen or broad accessibility behavior was not
exercised. Claim ceiling: a
compiled and loopback-API-smoked local implementation of a deterministic
synthetic quote preview and digest-bound synthetic approval contract; no buyer
authorization, seller identity, live availability, fulfillment, correctness,
payment, independent verification, or production claim. The next blocked
authority gate is a separately authorized live seller adapter and buyer
signer/identity model.

Next authority gate: separate product and operator authorization for seller
negotiation or real buyer signing. Fulfillment, verifier/dispute policy,
settlement, and production remain distinct later slices.

## `hyperai.bazaar_interface.synthetic_quote_completion.v1`

Status: implemented in the working tree. Focused Rust compilation, strict
Clippy, formatting, JavaScript syntax, and desktop browser smoke checks passed.
A loopback API smoke exercised completion, receipt verification, and
changed-digest rejection. Narrow-screen review, broader accessibility, and
automated contract tests remain open; this slice has no `INTERNAL_PASS` claim.

Baseline revision: `dcf41e31aa1f98438a6f8ec6cb253801e26dc0aa` on `main`;
implementation and proof-record changes are working-tree edits. Rust checks
used the repository-pinned Rust 1.93.1 toolchain.

Purpose: let a user continue the exact quote they reviewed and synthetically
approved into a seller-attributed fulfillment receipt, mock verifier decision,
and mock disposition. Recompute the fixture on the server and require both the
preview digest and buyer-approved deal digest before creating that receipt.

Included files:

- `crates/hyperai-market/src/lib.rs`: digest-checked completion over the
  existing synthetic quote, buyer approval, fulfillment, verifier, and mock
  settlement contracts.
- `crates/hyperai-application/src/lib.rs`: typed facade response binding the
  completion receipt back to the preview and approved deal.
- `crates/outcomes-cli/src/bin/hyperai-ui.rs`: loopback-only completion route.
- `apps/hyperai-interface/app.js` and `app.css`: separate user action after
  approval, linked receipt state, and explicit mock/no-funds labels.
- `README.md`, `docs/bazaar-hyperai-interface-plan.md`, and
  `docs/state-slices.md`: describe current local lifecycle and its limits.

Allowed effects: reconstruct the deterministic synthetic fixture; compare the
submitted preview and deal digests; and in memory, sign the synthetic seller
fulfillment statement, create the local mock verifier decision and mock
settlement record, and verify the complete receipt before returning it. Use
the fixture's simulated timestamps and keys only. No file, network, seller,
provider, agent, fleet, wallet, chain, evidence-publication, or funds effect is
permitted.

Non-goals: live negotiation, real buyer or seller identity, real signer
custody, workload execution, private inputs or outputs, real metering,
independent verification, dispute authority, escrow, payment, persistent deal
state, provider access, public evidence, or production readiness.

Claim ceiling: local demonstration that one deterministic quote preview and
synthetic approval digest can be carried into the existing mock lifecycle and
that the resulting receipt passes its local contract verifier. Seller
signature remains attribution to a fixture key; mock verifier and disposition
are not independent or real settlement evidence.

Proof gates: reject a changed preview or deal digest; bind the completion
receipt's approved deal to the exact recomputed digest; preserve seller
attribution, amount cap, timestamp, and receipt verification invariants; do
not expose the completion action before synthetic approval; show that the
completion step creates only a local mock record; and preserve loopback,
content-security, and memory-only behavior. `cargo check -p hyperai-market
-p hyperai-application -p outcomes-cli --all-targets`, strict Clippy for the
same packages, pinned-toolchain `rustfmt --check`, and `node --check` pass. A
loopback API smoke completed the mock lifecycle, verified its receipt, and
confirmed changed-preview or changed-deal rejection (`409`). A desktop browser

## `hyperai.bazaar.client_error_parity.v1`

Status: implemented; local proof gates passed on 2026-09-27 for this slice.
Assurance level: `INTERNAL_PASS`. Reviewer status: `NOT_REQUESTED`.
Reproducibility status: `NOT_REPRODUCED`.

This slice normalizes how the existing clients interpret local-service error
envelopes; it does not change authorization decisions, route semantics, or
error meanings.

Purpose: make browser, CLI, TUI, and ACP/MCP interpret the same
`hyperai.interface.error.v1` response consistently. Rust clients use one
application-owned decoder. Browser presentation validates schema, status, and code,
then displays a fixed generic message; it ignores response-body messages, so
message length and control characters cannot affect presentation. MCP/ACP
intentionally forwards only HTTP status and validated code; it never forwards
the service message or body. The CLI retains its existing exit-code mapping
and displays the normalized code and generic message; it does not display the
HTTP status.

Baseline: HyperAI `dcf41e31aa1f98438a6f8ec6cb253801e26dc0aa` on `main`, with
the existing dirty and untracked worktree. The Phase 1 and Phase 8 packets and
the Rust port subplan are present in this worktree.

Included files:

- `crates/hyperai-application/src/interface_error.rs` and
  `crates/hyperai-application/src/lib.rs`: shared error-envelope schema and
  decoder in the application contract layer.
- `crates/hyperai-tui/Cargo.toml`, `crates/hyperai-mcp/Cargo.toml`, and
  `crates/outcomes-cli/Cargo.toml`: depend directly on the shared contract
  layer instead of importing decoder code from the server.
- `Cargo.lock`: dependency edges for the direct application-contract imports;
  this lockfile already contained unrelated dirty baseline changes.
- `crates/hyperai-local-service/src/server.rs`: emit the shared error schema.
- `crates/hyperai-local-service/tests/api_contract.rs`: confirm the embedded
  browser decoder is served with the local shell.
- `crates/hyperai-tui/src/lib.rs`: decode service failures through the shared
  contract and retain the bounded diagnostic presentation.
- `crates/hyperai-mcp/src/lib.rs`: decode through the shared contract while
  continuing to omit the message and response body from ACP errors.
- `crates/outcomes-cli/src/lib.rs` and
  `crates/outcomes-cli/tests/cli_compat.rs`: normalize CLI service errors and
  cover malformed and valid synthetic envelopes.
- `apps/hyperai-interface/app.js`: validate and bound browser error fields
  before display.
- `apps/hyperai-interface/index.html` and
  `apps/hyperai-interface/error-envelope.js`: load a small browser error
  decoder before the interface entrypoint.
- `apps/hyperai-interface/error-envelope.test.mjs`: exercise the exact browser
  decoder with Node's built-in test runner.
- `docs/compute-bazaar-rust-port-subplan.md`: record the narrow result and
  remaining client-policy/accessibility gates.
- `docs/state-slices.md`: this scope and result record.

Allowed effects: local error-envelope parsing and presentation only, exercised
with synthetic request data and a temporary local home. A valid envelope must
use schema `hyperai.interface.error.v1`, status `error`, and a code of 1–80
ASCII uppercase letters, digits, underscores, or hyphens. Clients never trust
the response body's message; they use the service contract's fixed generic
message. Malformed, unknown-version, invalid-status, or invalid-code envelopes
fall back to `UNKNOWN_ERROR` and that same generic message. The actual HTTP
status remains authoritative. Browser, CLI, and TUI may show the normalized
message; MCP/ACP may expose only HTTP status and code.

Non-goals: changing server authorization or operation policy; changing route
methods, paths, payloads, status meanings, or success responses; exposing
request bodies, SQL, credentials, or service response bodies through ACP;
contacting a provider, seller, registry, agent, fleet, wallet, chain, or
reviewer; adding third-party dependencies or changing third-party versions;
changing source snapshots or data; or enabling
external effects, publication, or deployment.

Claim ceiling: local consistency of error-envelope decoding for the named
clients and synthetic cases only. It does not establish security against a
compromised local process, full client-policy parity, accessibility, clean
reproduction, cross-platform support, independent review, or production
readiness.

Proof gates: verify that valid synthetic failures preserve HTTP status in the
shared decoder and status-bearing clients, preserve the stable code across the
clients, and keep the CLI's existing exit-code mapping while ACP omits
message/body; verify malformed,
unknown-version, invalid-status, invalid-code, and malicious-message cases
fail closed; run the Node decoder test, focused service/CLI/TUI/MCP checks with
the pinned toolchain, browser-shell syntax validation, and an isolated local
browser/API smoke; run root `corepack pnpm run lint`; preserve unrelated dirty
work and report root and nested scopes separately. No external operations or
publishing are included.

Proof results (2026-09-27): the offline focused Rust suite passed 81 tests with
0 failures and 1 ignored packaged-sidecar test (it requires binaries staged by
`cargo build --workspace --bins`). The Node decoder suite passed 3 tests, and
`node --check` passed for both browser scripts. Root `corepack pnpm run lint`
passed formatting, strict all-target Clippy, contract tests, and the full
all-features workspace suite. The nested HyperIntel, JustAI, and Simple Compute
Market suites were not run because this slice changes only root-owned contracts
and clients; none of those product snapshots changed. In an isolated browser
smoke, the local shell
rendered Overview and Data; `/error-envelope.js` returned HTTP 200 with
`text/javascript; charset=utf-8`, and its served SHA-256 matched the workspace
asset (`52b74c23fdffe6971a0caa6584870387e77cabe289f61e20985cc59cb322d3ad`).
The temporary service, browser tab, and home were closed or removed afterward.

Data and artifact custody: only checked-out HyperAI source and fixed synthetic

## `hyperai.bazaar.acp_windows_process_ownership.v1`

Status: authorized local synthetic implementation and Windows-target
cross-compilation continuation under the user's direction to follow the Rust
compute-desk subplan and the accepted `hyperai.bazaar.acp.v1` slice. Native
Windows lifecycle qualification remains open; ACP support on Windows stays
disabled until that gate passes.

Baseline: HyperAI `dcf41e31aa1f98438a6f8ec6cb253801e26dc0aa` on `main`, plus
the existing dirty and untracked worktree. Preserve unrelated changes.

Purpose: ensure an explicitly started local ACP synthetic peer and its
descendants are owned and terminated as one unit on Windows. Use a Windows Job
Object with kill-on-close and no breakaway. Create the job before spawning the
peer; create the peer suspended, assign it to the job, and resume only after
assignment succeeds.

Exact files:

- `crates/hyperai-acp/Cargo.toml`: make `rustix` Unix-target-specific, add the
  exact optional Windows-target dependency `subc-jobobject = "=0.1.1"`, and
  keep its `windows-acp` feature disabled by default.
- `Cargo.lock`: lock the exact Windows-target dependency and checksum.
- `crates/hyperai-acp/src/session.rs`: preserve Unix process-group behavior;
  add Windows Job Object lifecycle and bounded tree termination without local
  unsafe code.
- `crates/hyperai-acp/tests/synthetic_peer.rs`: run the existing deterministic
  descendant-cleanup case on Unix and Windows and check platform process
  liveness.
- `docs/provenance.md`: record package identity, license, lockfile evidence,
  and the package metadata limitation.
- `docs/compute-bazaar-phase-8-acp-packet.md`: record the Windows process
  ownership design, tests, and native qualification gate.
- `docs/compute-bazaar-rust-port-subplan.md`: update Phase 8 status and limits.
- `docs/compute-bazaar-phase-1-contract-packet.md`: synchronize the desk
  platform matrix with the default-off Windows ACP implementation and native
  qualification gate.
- `docs/bazaar-hyperai-interface-plan.md`: synchronize its terminal/agent
  access boundary with the same ACP platform status.
- `docs/state-slices.md`: this exact authorization and evidence record.

Dependency review: `subc-jobobject` 0.1.1 is a crates.io package licensed MIT.
Its published metadata does not state an MSRV or repository URL. Its exact
source is reviewed from the registry archive and its checksum is bound by
`Cargo.lock`. Use its lower-level suspended-create, assign, resume, terminate,
and process-count operations. Do not use its `spawn_contained` convenience
function because it creates the Job Object after spawning the child. The root
workspace `unsafe_code = "forbid"` lint remains unchanged.

Allowed effects: start and stop only the HyperAI-authored synthetic peer in
local tests; build and test the ACP crate with the pinned Rust 1.93.1 toolchain;
and cross-compile the ACP crate and test targets for `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`
with the Windows feature both disabled and enabled. Tests use temporary
directories and fixed synthetic data. No third-party agent, provider, seller,
registry, remote Fleet, model, wallet, chain, external reviewer, or
non-synthetic payload is used.

Non-goals: enabling Windows ACP in product configuration; changing ACP v1
protocol negotiation, tool names, tool permissions, service routes, or
capability policy; changing Unix process supervision; weakening unsafe-code
lint; or claiming Windows process containment, a sandbox, external-agent
safety, or production readiness from cross-compilation.

Proof gates and results:

- `sh scripts/with-pinned-rust.sh cargo test --locked --offline -p
  hyperai-acp`: passed, 18 tests (9 unit and 9 synthetic-peer tests) on
  macOS arm64.
- `sh scripts/with-pinned-rust.sh cargo clippy --locked --offline -p
  hyperai-acp --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed on macOS arm64.
- Windows-target strict Clippy passed for
  `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`, both with the default feature set and with
  `--features windows-acp`.
- Locked offline all-target `cargo check` passed for
  `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`, both with the default feature set and with
  `--features windows-acp`.
- The Windows-target dependency tree excludes `subc-jobobject` by default and
  includes it only with `--features windows-acp`; no other workspace crate
  enables the feature.
- `sh scripts/with-pinned-rust.sh cargo fmt --all -- --check` and
  `git diff --check`: passed.

A native Windows run must exercise connect, disconnect, failed handshake,
cancellation, parent and descendant termination, and cleanup after
supervisor-task abort before Windows ACP can be enabled. This checkout has no
native Windows execution environment; cross-compilation does not satisfy that
gate.

Claim ceiling: local Unix behavior remains bounded by its existing evidence.
For Windows this slice can establish only source review, strict static checks,
and successful cross-target compilation until native execution is available.
It does not establish Windows runtime behavior or support, process containment
against hostile peers, a sandbox, independent review, or production
authorization. Assurance is `INTERNAL_PASS` only for the exact local synthetic
tests and static/cross-target checks; Windows runtime assurance remains
`NOT_ASSESSED`.

Reviewer status: `NOT_REQUESTED`. Reproducibility: `NOT_REPRODUCED`. Data and
artifact custody: HyperAI source, the checksum-locked MIT dependency, and

## `hyperai.bazaar.desk_runtime.restore_enospc_rollback.v1`

Status: complete for the named local test and root gates. The focused emulated
Linux `tmpfs` test passed twice in fresh containers from a clean disposable
target; root lint, pinned Rust formatting, import verification, and targeted
whitespace checks passed.

Purpose: exercise the public schema-v1 metadata restore path when the backing
filesystem runs out of space after the pre-restore safety snapshot succeeds.
The restore must report its safe recovery basename and, after tmpfs space is
released and the database is reopened, leave the pre-restore metadata and
schema unchanged. Preserve the `outcome_unknown` value reported at the error
boundary; SQLite can automatically roll back on `SQLITE_FULL`, in which case
an explicit rollback can return an error despite the unchanged database.

Exact files:

- `crates/hyperai-local-service/tests/storage.rs`: add one ignored Linux test
  using a size-limited `tmpfs`, an 8 MiB synthetic backup, and a physical
  `ENOSPC` condition during restore.
- `docs/compute-bazaar-phase-1-contract-packet.md`,
  `docs/compute-bazaar-rust-port-subplan.md`, and this record: capture the
  exact command, source and output digests, outcome, cleanup, assurance, and
  claim ceiling.

Allowed effects: run the focused ignored test with the pinned Rust 1.93.1
Linux/amd64 image, `--network none`, a read-only HyperAI source mount, a
read-only Cargo registry mount, a fresh disposable build target, and one
32 MiB `tmpfs` for the synthetic home and filler file. The test may write only
synthetic schema-v1 rows, a generated manual backup, the safety snapshot, and
the bounded filler file to that `tmpfs`. No host filesystem is filled.

Non-goals: production storage or API changes; host-disk exhaustion; other
platforms; power-loss testing; provider, registry, seller, agent, Fleet,
wallet, chain, reviewer, publication, or deployment effects; Bazaar source or
data reuse; nested-product edits; staging, commit, or release.

Proof gates: verify the configured test root is an exact 32 MiB `tmpfs`; write
the filler until Linux returns `ENOSPC`; preserve a valid manual backup whose
file size exceeds the 2 MiB space released for the restore; observe
`StorageError::RestoreFailed` with a safe pre-restore snapshot basename and
record its `outcome_unknown` value; confirm the safety snapshot exists; then
free the filler, close and reopen the databases, and verify the current
metadata rows still match their pre-restore values, the schema remains 1, the
selected backup bytes remain intact, and the safety snapshot contains the same
pre-restore values. Run the test twice in fresh containers, the root
`corepack pnpm run lint`, import verification, formatting, and diff hygiene.

Diagnostic failure: the first test version asserted that
`outcome_unknown = false`; that assertion failed. The focused follow-up kept
the reported value and inspected persisted state after freeing the filler.
Both passing runs reported 24,997,888 filler bytes written
before `ENOSPC`, 2,097,152 bytes reserved, an 8,540,160-byte manual backup, and
`outcome_unknown = true`. After freeing the filler and reopening the database,
the single pre-restore row, schema version 1, selected backup bytes, and safety
snapshot were intact. This is consistent with [SQLite's documented response
to transaction errors](https://www.sqlite.org/lang_transaction.html):
`SQLITE_FULL` can trigger automatic rollback, after which an explicit
`ROLLBACK` can itself return an error. The test preserves and reports that
uncertainty rather than treating the error value alone as proof of data loss.

`dcf41e31aa1f98438a6f8ec6b253801e26dc0aa` on `main`, plus the working-tree
source manifest covering root `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`, `.cargo/`, and all
regular files under `crates/`. The manifest has 107 files / 2,100,272 bytes;
its SHA-256 is
`13c34621099542dbf212ec71e3e3f526d483d0b18ab813e0638b2321a18649a3`. Each
sorted manifest record hashes the relative path, a NUL byte, the file SHA-256,
and a newline.

The test source SHA-256 is
`78cef9909fc0ad6e4d604a757c7cad327b73885dabb7a5841c6aaa3a04bfaac0`; the
locked `Cargo.lock` SHA-256 is
`b3708a2e0577a3e3d4a07c9110b33ae0ff0676b7aaaf495cf4278ba46e7e6736`; the
test binary SHA-256 is
`8a8334507d097158c721912c50042820fcd41c809a513f96449a39215856de47`; the

`b5f18e3bed474f74359e661b2a2027da491957ecffc17a25a8db6f9662c9bd09` and

container image was `rust:1.93.1-bookworm`,
`sha256:78a50754b62786434bc4ebfd874ef382348701b5f01b2c0d21b8e17cfad97969`,
with Rust 1.93.1. The first run compiled from a clean host target and the

reviewer status is `NOT_REQUESTED`; reproducibility is `NOT_REPRODUCED` because

stopped before page inspection.

fixed denied preview is excluded because it performs no Data read.
