`workload-trace.js`; `crates/hyperai-local-service/src/server.rs`; and the
existing synthetic Data seeding implementation. Exact editable files are this
packet, `docs/state-slices.md`, and
`docs/compute-bazaar-rust-port-subplan.md`; no application or test-code change
is authorized by this slice.

Allowed effects: build the current UI binary offline; run a disposable
loopback service at preflighted port 45239 with home
`/tmp/hyperai-browser-denied-parity-20260928`; seed only the fixed local
HyperAI sample through a separately launched headless Chromium process with
its own temporary profile; temporarily remove and restore read bits on its
JSON source; probe the owner route; and clean up only those temporary
resources. Bind DevTools to `127.0.0.1`, use loopback-only host resolver rules,
disable browser background networking, and run Chromium under a temporary
Seatbelt profile that denies all IP networking except outbound to port 45239
and bind/inbound operations on `127.0.0.1:45241` for DevTools. Permit Unix
domain socket bind/connect under the private run-owned browser temp root and
only under the `com.google.Chrome.*` subdirectory Chromium creates in the
current user's macOS temp directory. Keep those exceptions limited to Unix
domain socket operations; `TMPDIR` remains set to the private root for other
scratch files. Inspect DevTools request events and Chromium process sockets.
Stop if a non-loopback connection is attempted. Do not use the user's in-app
browser tabs or open Brave session. Preserve the existing listener on
`127.0.0.1:4317` (PID 85094). No external network or external data is allowed.

Proof gates: inspect the generated Seatbelt profile and preflight only local
service/DevTools connections and Unix sockets under both approved temporary
roots; confirm port availability and the isolated Chromium executable,
version, profile, and loopback-only DevTools endpoint;
verify the direct read
returns `PermissionDenied`; compare actual browser and owner-route status,
absent Data digest, and absent buyer-intent Data reference; check focus after
refresh, console errors, and desktop/narrow layouts; verify browser requests
and sockets stay on loopback; restore the file permission and verify the normal
state; stop and remove the test service, Chromium process group, profile, home,
and temporary logs; run root lint, import verification, diff, and whitespace
checks.

Diagnostic: the dedicated in-app browser blocked both numeric IPv4 loopback
and `localhost` navigation as `ERR_BLOCKED_BY_CLIENT` before the service saw a
request. This is a browser-client block and does not identify a product route
failure. Two isolated Chrome launches stopped before page load when Seatbelt
denied the Unix-domain process-singleton socket in macOS's per-user temporary
directory; setting `TMPDIR` did not redirect that socket. The scoped
`com.google.Chrome.*` Unix-socket exception then passed its local preflight.
Google Chrome 153.0.8010.53 reached the DevTools loopback listener but its
internal sandbox, network service, and GPU helpers failed under the outer
Seatbelt profile; the process exited with code 133 before a page result. Its
Crashpad report attempt was denied by Seatbelt, so the stop condition was
honored. No page request, UI action, Data seed, permission change, or owner
route comparison completed. The temporary browser profile, socket directory,
and test home were removed. The user's open Brave session and pre-existing
listener on port 4317 (PID 85094) were left untouched.

The later one-shot profile preflight rejected the numeric IP selector before
starting the app or Chrome: macOS Seatbelt accepts only `localhost` or `*` as
a network-rule host. The original numeric-address retry is closed as
`INCONCLUSIVE`; no page request, UI action, Data seed, permission change, or
owner-route comparison completed. The already installed Chrome 153 binary and
its diagnostic flags are carried into a separate, explicitly named
continuation slice below. No browser result is claimed here.

only; the actual browser gate is `INCONCLUSIVE` and the denied state is

runtime files. The actual browser gate remains open pending the one controlled

## `hyperai.bazaar.data_sql_scalar_function_modifiers.v1`

Status: `INTERNAL_PASS` for the exact local synthetic parser/API cases below.
Reviewer status is `NOT_REQUESTED`; reproducibility is `NOT_REPRODUCED`. The
slice closes a pinned parser/planner mismatch for the allowlisted scalar SQL
functions.

Baseline: HyperAI `dcf41e31aa1f98438a6f8ec6b253801e26dc0aa` on `main`, plus
the existing dirty and untracked worktree. Preserve unrelated work and the
pre-existing service on port 4317.

Source basis: `sqlparser 0.59.0` `GenericDialect` parses scalar `FILTER`,
null-treatment, and function-argument clauses. In DataFusion 52.5.0,
`FunctionArgs::try_new` separates those fields, while the scalar-function
metadata branch builds a `ScalarFunction` from ordinary arguments and returns
without applying those modifiers. The Data validator must not approve a query
whose parsed modifier can be discarded by that planner path.

Exact files:

- `crates/hyperai-data/src/lib.rs`: reject parsed scalar function
  `FILTER`/null-treatment modifiers and nonempty argument clauses for the
  allowlisted scalar functions; add exact AST and compatibility regressions.
- `crates/hyperai-local-service/tests/data_api.rs`: require HTTP 422 and
  `DATA_QUERY_REJECTED` for the three fixed scalar modifier requests.
- `docs/state-slices.md`: record scope, threat model, validation, and limits.
- `docs/compute-bazaar-phase-2-data-packet.md`: record the pinned source
  mismatch and evidence.
- `docs/compute-bazaar-rust-port-subplan.md`: update Phase 2 parser status.

Allowed effects: use only these fixed SQL strings against the pinned parser
and existing validator/test harness; run the focused `hyperai-data` and
authenticated `data_api` tests, Rust formatting, root `corepack pnpm run lint`,
and scoped Markdown hygiene. API cases run on the test-owned ephemeral loopback
service and disposable home and are rejected before planning or dataset scan.
The existing service on port 4317 remains untouched.

Cases: reject `ABS(amount) FILTER (WHERE amount < 0)`,
`ABS(amount) IGNORE NULLS`, and `ABS(amount ORDER BY amount)`; preserve ordinary
`ABS(amount)` and aggregate `SUM(amount) FILTER (WHERE amount > 0)` validation.

Non-goals: execute any case-specific query; read or modify a dataset; change
the SQL dialect, function allowlist, DataFusion version, API schema,
authentication, storage, result limits, or aggregate modifier behavior; add a
dependency; or connect a provider, source, reviewer, wallet, chain, or
production system.

Threat model: an authenticated local caller supplies SQL. The relevant abuse
path is a scalar modifier represented by the parser AST but dropped by the
planner, causing a query to be accepted with different semantics. Controls
are a pre-planning validator guard, exact AST-field assertions, aggregate
compatibility checks, and API status/code assertions.

Proof gates: each SQL form parses into the expected AST field; the three
scalar forms return `QueryRejected`; ordinary scalar and aggregate-filter
forms remain in the documented subset; the authenticated API returns HTTP 422
with `DATA_QUERY_REJECTED`; focused tests, formatting, root lint, and scoped
Markdown hygiene pass; no dataset scan or existing-service access occurs.

`DATA_QUERY_REJECTED` for all three scalar modifier cases. Pinned Rust

for `crates/hyperai-data/src/lib.rs` and
`4978725d7eef4a8661876d6cee2e7c127d1340c9b20540285c60691e2a341dd3` for

## `hyperai.bazaar.data_sql_scalar_distinct.v1`

Status: `INTERNAL_PASS` for the exact local synthetic parser/API case below.
Reviewer status is `NOT_REQUESTED`; reproducibility is `NOT_REPRODUCED`. This
slice addresses one pinned parser/planner mismatch for `DISTINCT` on
allowlisted scalar calls.

Baseline: HyperAI `dcf41e31aa1f98438a6f8ec6b253801e26dc0aa` on `main`, plus
the existing dirty and untracked worktree. Preserve unrelated work and the
pre-existing service on port 4317.

Source basis: `sqlparser 0.59.0` stores `DISTINCT` in
`FunctionArgumentList.duplicate_treatment`. DataFusion 52.5.0 extracts that
field into `FunctionArgs.distinct`, but its scalar-expression path constructs
a `ScalarFunction` from the ordinary arguments without applying `distinct`.
The local Data validator must reject a parsed scalar form whose modifier the
planner can discard.

Exact files:

- `crates/hyperai-data/src/lib.rs`: reject nonempty scalar
  `duplicate_treatment`; assert the exact parser field and preserve ordinary
  scalar plus aggregate-distinct validation.
- `crates/hyperai-local-service/tests/data_api.rs`: require HTTP 422 and
  `DATA_QUERY_REJECTED` for the fixed scalar `DISTINCT` request.
- `docs/state-slices.md`: record scope, threat model, validation, and limits.
- `docs/compute-bazaar-phase-2-data-packet.md`: record the pinned
  parser/planner mismatch and evidence.
- `docs/compute-bazaar-rust-port-subplan.md`: update Phase 2 parser status.

Allowed effects: use only `SELECT ABS(DISTINCT gpu_model) FROM dataset`,
`SELECT ABS(gpu_model) FROM dataset`, and
`SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT gpu_model) FROM dataset` against the pinned parser,
validator, and authenticated local API test harness; run the focused Data and
`data_api` tests, pinned Rust formatting, root `corepack pnpm run lint`, and
scoped Markdown hygiene. Reject the scalar case before planning or dataset
access. Keep the existing service on port 4317 untouched.

Non-goals: execute any case-specific query; read or modify a dataset; change
the SQL dialect, allowlist, DataFusion version, API schema, authentication,
storage, result limits, or aggregate-distinct behavior; add a dependency; or
connect a provider, source, reviewer, wallet, chain, or production system.

Threat model: an authenticated local caller supplies SQL. A scalar function's
parsed `DISTINCT` modifier can be extracted by the planner and then dropped,
allowing the validator to approve syntax whose requested semantics are not
represented in the resulting scalar expression. Controls are a pre-planning
guard, exact AST-field assertion, aggregate compatibility assertion, and
authenticated API status/code assertion.

Proof gates: the parser populates `duplicate_treatment` as `Distinct`; scalar
`ABS(DISTINCT ...)` returns `QueryRejected`; plain `ABS(...)` and aggregate
`COUNT(DISTINCT ...)` remain in the validator's accepted subset; the API
returns HTTP 422 with `DATA_QUERY_REJECTED`; focused tests, formatting, root
lint, and scoped Markdown hygiene pass; no dataset read or existing-service
access occurs.

Implementation evidence (2026-09-29): the focused `hyperai-data` suite passed
38 tests. The authenticated `data_api` regression
`query_api_rejects_unregistered_functions_and_cancel_unknown_query` passed
(1 passed, 0 failed, 2 filtered), including HTTP 422 and
`DATA_QUERY_REJECTED` for scalar `ABS(DISTINCT ...)`. Pinned formatting,
strict workspace Clippy, contract tests, and the full all-feature workspace
test/doc-test gate completed through `corepack pnpm run lint` with exit 0.
The source SHA-256 values are
`fe7ba3ce69a482247a680340fe8a4731893cb596e9a72d199dbec42c524ea65c` for
`crates/hyperai-data/src/lib.rs` and
`6ad9dd2546eb99ed3b7dd3b6c642d886f72227226b9afa5a889fde41cfd24d40` for
`crates/hyperai-local-service/tests/data_api.rs`. Only fixed SQL literals
were used; no dataset was read and the pre-existing service was untouched.

Claim ceiling: rejection of this exact parsed scalar `DISTINCT` form while
preserving the tested ordinary scalar and aggregate-distinct forms. This does
not establish complete SQL security, exhaustive parser coverage, planner
equivalence, DataFusion memory isolation, independent review, or overall Phase

not implied. Overall Phase 2 remains `NOT_ASSIGNED` until its full packet gates
are met. Publish boundary: local source and synthetic evidence only.

## `hyperai.bazaar.data_sql_distinct_on_planner_mismatch.v1`

Status: completed local synthetic parser/planner compatibility slice;
`INTERNAL_PASS` for the exact parser/API regressions and root validation.
Overall Phase 2 Data acceptance remains `NOT_ASSIGNED`.

Baseline: HyperAI `dcf41e31aa1f98438a6f8ec6cb253801e26dc0aa` on `main`, plus
the existing dirty and untracked worktree. Preserve all unrelated paths and the
existing service on `127.0.0.1:4317`.

Purpose: reject `DISTINCT ON` at SQL validation. The pinned `sqlparser 0.59.0`
`GenericDialect` parser represents both empty and nonempty forms as
`Distinct::On`. DataFusion `52.5.0` has a logical-planner path for nonempty
expressions, but executing the local nonempty query fails in optimizer rule
`replace_distinct_aggregate` because `first_value` is absent from this
workspace's function registry. The empty form also fails during planning.
HyperAI maps these planner failures to `QueryFailed`, which the local API
reports as an internal operation failure. Rejecting the unsupported AST
variant before dataset lookup preserves the established query-rejection
contract without changing the DataFusion feature set.

Exact files:

- `crates/hyperai-data/src/lib.rs`: reject every `Distinct::On` variant
  during validation and assert the exact parsed AST for empty and nonempty
  forms.
- `crates/hyperai-data/tests/query_contract.rs`: prove empty and nonempty
  `DISTINCT ON` forms return `QueryRejected` before touching an unseeded data
  root, while ordinary `DISTINCT` still executes over the synthetic snapshot.
- `crates/hyperai-local-service/tests/data_api.rs`: require HTTP 422 and
  `DATA_QUERY_REJECTED` for empty and nonempty forms through the existing
  authenticated rejection route while its disposable service home has no
  seeded dataset.
- `docs/state-slices.md`: this scope and its evidence.
- `docs/compute-bazaar-phase-2-data-packet.md`: pinned parser/planner behavior,
  result, and limits.
- `docs/compute-bazaar-rust-port-subplan.md`: update the bounded Phase 2
  parser progress summary only.

Allowed effects: parse fixed HyperAI-authored empty and nonempty
`DISTINCT ON` cases and standard `DISTINCT` with the pinned parser; reject both
`DISTINCT ON` forms before planning; execute ordinary `DISTINCT` against a
freshly seeded HyperAI synthetic dataset in a disposable test root; exercise
the existing authenticated local API against its unseeded temporary home; run
the focused package/API tests, pinned formatting, root lint, and scoped
Markdown hygiene. No test may contact or stop the pre-existing service.

Non-goals: change the SQL dialect, broaden the accepted syntax, alter ordinary
or aggregate `DISTINCT`, modify DataFusion or SQLparser versions, change query
limits, storage, API schemas, authentication, datasets, or other parser rules;
add dependencies; connect external sources/providers; access persistent user
data; use network, paid work, external writes, publication, or production.

Threat model: an authenticated local caller supplies SQL. `DISTINCT ON`
passes the current AST policy, but its pinned DataFusion optimizer path fails
for the local workspace configuration. Mapping those failures to
`QueryFailed` misclassifies unsupported syntax as an accepted operation
failure. The control is a pre-planning AST check, an ordinary `DISTINCT`
compatibility test, and authenticated API status/code assertions in an
unseeded home.

Proof gates: the parser populates `Distinct::On` for empty and nonempty forms;
validation returns `QueryRejected` for both; standard `DISTINCT` remains
accepted and executes over the synthetic snapshot; the API returns HTTP 422
with `DATA_QUERY_REJECTED` for both forms before dataset lookup; the focused
tests, formatting, root lint, and scoped documentation checks pass.

Validation on macOS 26.6.1 arm64 with pinned Rust/Cargo 1.93.1: locked offline
`hyperai-data --all-targets` passed 40 tests (25 unit, 5 catalog, 2 derived
data, 8 query contract); the named authenticated `data_api` regression passed
(1 passed, 0 failed, 2 filtered); pinned formatting and
`CARGO_NET_OFFLINE=true corepack pnpm run lint` passed, including strict
Clippy, workspace contract tests, all-feature tests, and doc tests. The
all-feature run retained its existing environment-gated ignored tests. Source
SHA-256 values are `3cc24a59e14a9d1d3412adfc1676462135a59419d6b7655c625c96799fe44689`
for `crates/hyperai-data/src/lib.rs`,
`fb715312bae4258f931fb3831f55ea9c78856509fa259b683e1ef7147454ba51` for
`crates/hyperai-data/tests/query_contract.rs`, and
`0b6b96da1c81e0144029322e48c91f822271aee6a3a97393fd3448402de5fcd9` for
`crates/hyperai-local-service/tests/data_api.rs`.

Claim ceiling: pre-planning rejection of the tested `DISTINCT ON` forms and
preservation of ordinary `DISTINCT` for the local synthetic query contract.
This does not establish exhaustive SQL safety, general planner equivalence,

## `hyperai.bazaar.data_output_size_preflight.v1`

Status: authorized bounded local continuation under the user's direction to
follow the Compute Bazaar Rust port subplan. Baseline is HyperAI
`dcf41e31aa1f98438a6f8ec6cb253801e26dc0aa` plus the existing dirty and
untracked working tree. Assurance overlay:
`global-experiment-assurance-lifecycle-v1`.

Purpose: make bounded query-result accounting incremental and reject an
over-limit encoded row before retaining it in the result. The current code
re-serializes all accumulated rows after each row and pushes the row before
checking the 256 KiB ceiling. The continuation must preserve the existing
JSON/CSV output encoding and exact accepted-query results.

Exact files:

- `crates/hyperai-data/src/lib.rs`: add bounded encoded-cell counting,
  incremental row-size accounting, and deterministic regressions.
- `docs/compute-bazaar-phase-2-data-packet.md`: record the implementation
  evidence, measurement scope, and remaining Phase 2 gates.
- `docs/compute-bazaar-rust-port-subplan.md`: append the bounded Phase 2
  continuation summary only.

Allowed effects: use the pinned local DataFusion/Arrow formatter and
HyperAI-authored in-memory arrays; change only the listed query collector,
its tests, and documentation; run locked/offline focused Data checks, pinned

documentation hygiene. Do not contact the pre-existing service on
`127.0.0.1:4317`.

Non-goals: changing SQL syntax or policy, query limits, API schemas, result
encoding, dependencies, input snapshots, source adapters, datasets, client
behavior, other workspaces, or the DataFusion memory-pool configuration;
reading non-synthetic data; provider, seller, Fleet, paid Eval, financial
Trade, payment, settlement, network, publication, release, or production
activity; and claiming a whole-process memory bound.

Threat model: row-by-row full-result serialization has quadratic work as the
result grows. Checking after row insertion allows partial in-memory mutation
and transient retention above the advertised result ceiling. Formatting
repeated large columns before checking the encoded size can also allocate an
oversized row outside DataFusion's pool. The new preflight must count the
exact existing JSON/CSV cell representation without first materializing a
formatted cell string, then materialize and append only if the row fits.

Proof gates: for JSON and CSV, the bounded counter matches the current
serializer for nulls, quotes, backslashes, control characters, delimiters,
newlines, carriage returns, and UTF-8; a result exactly at the byte ceiling
is accepted; an additional byte is rejected without changing prior rows or
the committed size counter; ordinary accepted rows remain byte-identical;
the locked/offline Data package suite, pinned formatting, root offline lint,
import preservation, and scoped documentation hygiene pass; out-of-slice
paths remain unchanged.

Claim ceiling: exact incremental byte accounting and no over-limit row
retention for the tested JSON/CSV cases on the pinned local toolchain. This
does not establish complete process-memory or CPU bounds, accounting of every
DataFusion allocation, exhaustive SQL safety, independent review, clean
second-environment reproduction, external data rights, or full Phase 2
acceptance. Reviewer status is `NOT_REQUESTED`; reproduction starts as
`NOT_REPRODUCED`. Publish boundary: local source and documentation only.

source-specific rights and retention decisions before non-synthetic reads.

response is rejected. The illustrative byte totals are not asserted as the
exact Rust fixture's serialized size.

probe. The root `pnpm run lint` run reached the all-feature workspace tests and

request path; it does not establish the OS-level cause of every prior failure.

selected as the smallest change matching the bytes the request already sends;

fixture and the test-local mutex already failed to prevent recurrence.

## `hyperai.bazaar.data_query_process_isolation_design.v1`

Status: authorized documentation-only architecture continuation under the
user-directed Compute Desk subplan and
`global-experiment-assurance-lifecycle-v1`. It defines a design gate for
possible future query-worker isolation; it does not authorize implementation.

Baseline: HyperAI `dcf41e31aa1f98438a6f8ec6cb253801e26dc0aa` on `main`, plus
the preserved dirty and untracked worktree. Pre-change SHA-256 values:

- `docs/state-slices.md`:
  `ca365f4df0a38f90f7aff422a5db61d343d7b65f7d167c15d4b6e31acc2947e5`
- `docs/compute-bazaar-phase-2-data-packet.md`:
  `a368338feff731d17b54bdc513e7c350c4e6e2d7fd34a314bed3e23091957aae`
- `docs/compute-bazaar-rust-port-subplan.md`:
  `823e75994b7e7851f75df62e7d0b4800712212fd5ac27ec1a73bab78cf53eead`

Exact writable files are limited to this record,
`docs/compute-bazaar-phase-2-data-packet.md`, and
`docs/compute-bazaar-rust-port-subplan.md`.

Purpose: turn the remaining DataFusion resource-isolation risk into a
platform-aware implementation gate while preserving the single HyperAI
service/API contract. Current query memory-pool configuration, API
concurrency, measured RSS, and a process-level memory limit are separate
controls and must continue to be reported separately.

Allowed effects: documentation edits only and read-only consultation of
official Apache DataFusion, Linux kernel, and Microsoft Windows documentation.
No tests or binaries run; no subprocess, service, dataset, network endpoint,
or external source is contacted by the product.

Proposed architecture to evaluate in a later implementation slice:

- Keep authentication, caller authorization, SQL validation, catalog and
  manifest checks, source-path confinement, request caps, API error mapping,
  and durable metadata in the existing HyperAI service and application layer.
- If selected, execute each bounded query in a supervised worker with a
  versioned bounded IPC contract. The worker receives only the already
  authorized query and one immutable digest-bound snapshot; it gets no general
  HyperAI home access, credentials, network, or authority to alter records.
- Keep the DataFusion memory pool and one-partition policy inside the worker
  as query-engine controls. Independently enforce and measure an operating
  system limit on the worker or its containment group. The existing two-slot
  API admission limit bounds concurrency only.
- The parent owns wall-time cancellation, worker termination and wait/reap,
  bounded stderr/result handling, complete-response validation, and the rule
  that a crash, timeout, or partial response never becomes success. Only
  report a resource-limit error when the platform evidence identifies that
  cause; otherwise preserve an unknown worker failure.
- Do not enable a claimed bounded-worker mode on a platform until native tests
  establish limit enforcement, cancellation, crash recovery, cleanup, and
  combined service-plus-worker capacity. Linux cgroup v2 exposes `memory.max`
  for a cgroup; Windows Job Objects can group processes and impose a job-wide
  committed-memory limit. No macOS enforcement mechanism is selected or
  qualified by this design; a platform spike must resolve it before macOS can
  claim the worker memory bound. The native v3 probe then measured a
  `TASK_VM_INFO.virtual_size` baseline of 445,746,020,352 bytes, set soft
  `RLIMIT_AS` 64 MiB above it, and observed one 128 MiB allocation refused
  with `ENOMEM`; raw `ru_maxrss=1392640` does not establish an RSS limit. This
  makes `RLIMIT_AS` unsuitable as the selected macOS worker memory budget for
  the observed process baseline. Keep macOS worker enforcement unresolved and
  unclaimed pending a separate native mechanism spike.
- Preserve current API and CLI/TUI/browser contracts unless a separate slice
  explicitly versions them. Bazaar rights, external data, provider calls,
  paid work, federation, settlement, publication, and deployment remain out
  of scope.

Proof gates for this documentation slice: the packet and subplan distinguish
DataFusion memory-pool accounting, service concurrency, measured RSS, and OS
enforcement; name the parent/worker authority boundary and lifecycle; identify
the platform-specific proof still required; and make no implementation,
capacity, or production claim. The official references consulted are
[DataFusion runtime configuration](https://datafusion.apache.org/user-guide/configs.html),
[Linux cgroup v2](https://docs.kernel.org/admin-guide/cgroup-v2.html),
[Windows Job Objects](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/procthread/job-objects),
and the [Windows job-wide committed-memory limit](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winnt/ns-winnt-jobobject_basic_limit_information).

Claim ceiling: `PLANNING_ONLY`; this is a proposed architecture and a set of
future proof gates, not evidence that a worker, sandbox, process-memory bound,
or supported-platform implementation exists. Reviewer status is
`NOT_REQUESTED`; reproducibility is `NOT_APPLICABLE`. Data and artifact
custody are the named HyperAI documentation files and the cited public
technical references and the linked synthetic native probe packet. Next gate:
define and separately authorize an alternative macOS resource-enforcement
spike plus exact IPC/lifecycle contract before changing runtime code. Publish
boundary: local documentation only; no commit, PR, release, or deployment.

## `hyperai.bazaar.data_macos_rlimit_probe.v1`

Status: authorized one-run, local synthetic platform probe under the
user-directed Compute Desk subplan and
`global-experiment-assurance-lifecycle-v1`. This tests one candidate native
resource-control mechanism; it does not authorize Data worker implementation.

Baseline: HyperAI `dcf41e31aa1f98438a6f8ec6cb253801e26dc0aa` on `main`, plus
the preserved dirty and untracked worktree. Host observed before execution:
macOS `26.6.1`, `arm64`, Apple clang `21.0.0`. Pre-change SHA-256 values:

- `docs/state-slices.md`:
  `81c12bf2d69cab7ba1f3a736b1b0950a653482544b35c5f65823b39f533ebe34`
- `docs/compute-bazaar-phase-2-data-packet.md`:
  `d242b843ed402715ebfc70c2492314952b3b610d78bf579e5c7da6cb6c535774`
- `docs/compute-bazaar-rust-port-subplan.md`:
  `c48cf9360478bf949ec2ec5e5fcd3184d2b0a64442596e5917e12c905608820a`

Exact writable repository files are limited to this record,
`docs/compute-bazaar-data-macos-resource-limit-probe.md`,
`docs/compute-bazaar-phase-2-data-packet.md`, and
`docs/compute-bazaar-rust-port-subplan.md`.

Purpose: determine whether this exact native macOS environment enforces a
child process's `RLIMIT_AS` limit strongly enough to warrant a later DataFusion
worker spike. Apple's current XNU headers define `RLIMIT_AS` and alias
`RLIMIT_RSS` to it, while the available Apple manual page describes resource
limits; these references motivate a probe and are not runtime evidence.

Allowed effects: compile one fixed C helper from standard input into an
automatically removed temporary directory using `/usr/bin/cc`; run it once as
a child process; capture its exit status, bounded output, binary digest, and
reported peak RSS; then remove the temporary directory. The helper reads and
lowers only its own soft `RLIMIT_AS` to 128 MiB, requests a fixed 192 MiB
allocation, touches at most one byte per system page, reports allocation and
`getrusage` results, and exits. It makes no file, network, service, account,
or host resource-limit changes. The packet records the exact helper source and
command. Any setup error, signal, timeout, or ambiguous output is preserved as
`INCONCLUSIVE`; do not repeat it in this slice.

Non-goals: compiling or running Rust/DataFusion, changing product code, testing
other macOS versions or hardware, installing packages, reading user data,
contacting an external source, changing a parent/shell limit, or claiming a
general sandbox or worker-memory guarantee.

Proof gates: verify the exact host/toolchain, exact `RLIMIT_AS` request and
result, attempted allocation size, child exit or signal, and peak-RSS reporting;
hash the helper binary; remove every temporary artifact; compare repository
status and the three pre-existing import pins before and after. Interpret an
allocation refusal only as evidence that this child could not allocate this
fixed block under this limit. A passing allocation is evidence that this
candidate did not enforce the attempted bound. Neither result establishes
DataFusion startup, query behavior, RSS enforcement, or supported-platform
qualification.

Execution result (2026-10-01): `INCONCLUSIVE`. The exact host was macOS
`26.6.1` arm64 with Apple clang `21.0.0`. The temporary helper compiled with
exit 0; binary SHA-256 was

Purpose: reject duplicate dataset identities in the local manifest directory.
The current catalog reads every `.json` entry, gathers its embedded ID, and
reopens the canonical manifest for that ID. A copied alias manifest can
therefore make one valid dataset appear twice and leave the owner status
classified as `bound`. Reject the duplicate ID as `InvalidCatalog`; the owner
status must then fail closed as `conflicting` without exposing a digest.

Exact writable files:

- `crates/hyperai-data/src/lib.rs`: reject adjacent duplicate dataset IDs
  after sorting the manifest identities.
- `crates/hyperai-data/tests/catalog_contract.rs`: add a disposable-home
  alias-manifest regression for both the catalog and owner status projection.
- `docs/compute-bazaar-data-manifest-catalog-redteam-packet.md`: record the
  threat boundary, finding, fix, proof, and residual limits.
- `docs/compute-bazaar-rust-port-subplan.md`: record the Data catalog
  integrity correction and its narrow claim ceiling.
- `docs/state-slices.md`: this authorization and result.

Allowed effects: create the two fixed synthetic manifests in a temporary
home; copy one manifest to an alias `.json` entry inside that same home; run
the focused offline `hyperai-data` catalog test, pinned format check, root
`lint:fast`, import verification, and documentation hygiene checks. No
service, user home, external source, network, provider, seller, model, Fleet,
paid Eval, financial Trade, wallet, chain, or reviewer is contacted.

Bounded red-team model: an untrusted or corrupted extra JSON manifest may be
present under the selected local `manifests/` directory. The tested abuse goal
is duplicate catalog identity or a false `bound` Data reference. The fixed
dataset-ID allowlist, exact relative-path allowlist, root canonicalization,
symlink rejection, content digest, and size bounds remain in force. This
review does not test a same-user concurrent path-swap race, malicious
filesystem behavior, manifest-count exhaustion, or other operating systems.

Non-goals: changing manifest/API schemas, adding datasets or source adapters,
altering accepted relative paths, changing query behavior, changing Activity
or Market history, or upgrading the earlier unavailable-state slice's
assurance disposition. Phase 2 worker isolation and source-rights gates remain
separate.

Proof gates: the regression first demonstrates that the duplicate alias is
accepted on the frozen baseline, then verifies catalog rejection and `conflicting`
owner-status mapping after the fix; existing path-mutation tests remain
unchanged; the focused Data package test and pinned formatting pass; root
`lint:fast`, import verification, `git diff --check`, and authored-file
whitespace checks pass; temporary roots are removed and no file is staged.

Claim ceiling: local synthetic manifest identity rejection and the bounded
source review described here only. Target assurance is `INTERNAL_PASS` for
these tests and the review if every proof gate passes. Reviewer status is
`NOT_REQUESTED`; reproduction is `NOT_REPRODUCED`. No external data, source
rights, broad filesystem security, independent review, platform support,
worker isolation, or production readiness is established.

Publish boundary: local source and docs only; no commit, PR, external
circulation, release, deployment, or production operation.

## `hyperai.bazaar.gpudiff_live_offer_snapshot.v1`

Status: bounded implementation and local E2E qualification completed under
`INTERNAL_PASS` for this slice only. This is a fresh source-specific
continuation of `hyperai.bazaar.data_local.v1`; it does not reopen the
synthetic-only contract or authorize compute-market execution.

Purpose: let the local owner explicitly fetch and import one snapshot from
GPUDiff's public GPU-offer feed so the existing HyperAI Data catalog, bounded
SQL query, and browser workspace can be exercised with non-synthetic,
source-attributed records. GPUDiff is an aggregator, not the underlying GPU
provider. Keep its record-level provider/source attribution and observed time;
do not turn these rows into HyperAI offers, procurement eligibility, a price
index, a quote, or dispatch input.

Baseline: HyperAI `dcf41e31aa1f98438a6f8ec6cb253801e26dc0aa` on `main`, with
the pre-existing dirty and untracked worktree preserved. Source selected on
2026-10-05: `https://gpudiff.com/api/v1/offers.json`, whose published data is
CC BY 4.0 with attribution to `gpudiff.com`. A read-only HEAD returned HTTP
200, `Content-Length: 1591997`, ETag `6ac3ebb2-184abd`, and
`Last-Modified: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 18:25:54 GMT`. These headers are observations,
not a frozen content identity; the implementation must hash the exact GET
body and bind each import to that digest.

Exact writable files:

- `crates/hyperai-data/src/lib.rs`: bounded GPUDiff V1 payload validation,
  source digest and receipt, normalized immutable snapshot, catalog/query
  support, and idempotent local persistence.
- `crates/hyperai-data/tests/gpudiff_snapshot_contract.rs`: fixed parser,
  size, malformed-record, fixture-exclusion, digest, idempotency, and recovery
  cases using an explicitly synthetic contract fixture; no network calls.
- `crates/hyperai-application/src/lib.rs`: typed import facade that keeps the
  external source separate from market selection, settlement, and outcomes.
- `crates/hyperai-local-service/src/server.rs`: one owner-only refresh route
  with a fixed HTTPS endpoint, no caller-supplied URL, and bounded outbound
  response handling. It must not be available through ACP/MCP agent routes.
- `crates/hyperai-local-service/tests/data_api.rs`: route authorization,
  idempotency, catalog, and query contract checks using local test responses.
- `apps/hyperai-interface/app.js`: an explicit owner action to fetch the
  public snapshot and show its source, freshness, digest, and nonclaims.
- `docs/compute-bazaar-route-auth-effect-inventory-v1.md`: add the route and
  its owner-only network-read/local-write effect.
- `docs/compute-bazaar-gpudiff-live-offer-packet-v1.md`: source contract,
  implementation evidence, and exact live-test results for this slice.
- `docs/state-slices.md`: this authorization and evidence record.

Allowed effects: a user-triggered HTTPS GET to the exact GPUDiff URL above,
followed by local immutable snapshot and receipt writes beneath the selected
HyperAI data root. Send no account data, request payload, credential, or
provider request. The request has a 10-second deadline, no automatic retry,
no redirect, a 4 MiB source-body ceiling, and a 4,096-record ceiling. Reject a
missing/oversized content length, invalid content type, non-200 response,
invalid JSON, unsupported schema, empty response, or any source row marked as
a fixture. Bound normalized output by the existing 16 MiB Data limit. Keep at
most 16 distinct source captures (4 MiB each) and stop with a typed limit error
instead of deleting prior evidence. Identical source bytes are an idempotent
success; changed data creates a new digest-bound snapshot and advances the
catalog's current GPUDiff snapshot atomically. Refresh is user initiated; no
background polling, subscription, websocket, provider call, paid action, or
automatic retry is included.

The exact source body is retained locally under a digest-derived path. Each
normalized row preserves the source offer ID, provider label, GPU/SKU fields,
original price and unit, pricing type, region, publisher attributes, source
URL, and source observation time. It also binds the raw source SHA-256. The
receipt records the endpoint, response ETag/Last-Modified when present, raw
digest, normalized snapshot digest, import time, attribution, and retention
policy. Do not commit the live payload, source receipt, generated rows, or
other data artifacts to the repository.

Non-goals: provider authentication or direct provider connections; a
continuous stream or scheduler; live offer revalidation; normalization into
`hyperai-market::Offer`; seller identity or capacity verification; provider
execution; quote, deal, settlement, outcome, or payment effects; public
publication; changing existing synthetic data semantics; modifying imported
HyperIntel, JustAI, SCM, or Bazaar snapshots; staging, committing, opening a
PR, or deployment.

Proof gates: focused offline tests cover exact decimal-to-micros conversion,
record/schema limits, duplicate or malformed source data rejection,
fixture rejection, digest binding, no-overwrite conflict handling, atomic
manifest replacement, and idempotency. Run the locked `hyperai-data` and
`hyperai-local-service` focused tests, formatting/Clippy for touched Rust
packages, root interface verification, import verification, and diff hygiene.
Then make one live read through the owner route in a temporary HyperAI home;
confirm a non-empty non-fixture snapshot appears in `/api/v1/data/catalog`,
verify its raw source digest, and execute bounded DataFusion SQL against the
same dataset ID. Capture only response status, source/normalized digests,
row count, observed-time range, and query result count; do not retain the live
payload in test output. Clean the temporary home and confirm the pre-existing
user home was not touched.

Claim ceiling: a local snapshot of the exact GPUDiff public payload, with
GPUDiff-reported provider/source fields and timestamps. It does not establish
direct provider access, an executable offer, present or guaranteed capacity,
provider endorsement, correct computation, price representativeness, buyer
eligibility, payment entitlement, or production readiness. Expected assurance
after scoped local checks is `INTERNAL_PASS`; reviewer status
`NOT_REQUESTED`; reproduction status `NOT_REPRODUCED`; independent review and
production authorization remain closed.

Publish boundary: local source and local user-owned data only. The source
license requires attribution to `gpudiff.com`; the UI and local receipt must
retain it. No public release or external publication.

Implementation and evidence (2026-10-05): source revision
`dcf41e31aa1f98438a6f8ec6cb253801e26dc0aa` plus the scoped, uncommitted
working-tree changes listed above. The owner-only `POST
/api/v1/data/gpudiff/refresh` made one fixed HTTPS request, and the live test
confirmed HTTP 200 for refresh, HTTP 401 without owner authentication, a
matching catalog digest, and five bounded DataFusion query rows. The exact
source and normalized digests, response size, row count, observation range,
and query result count are recorded in the GPUDiff packet. The ignored live
test used a temporary HyperAI home, which was removed at test completion; no
source payload or generated record was written to the repository.

The three offline parser/import tests passed, including exact decimal
conversion, malformed/duplicate/fixture rejection, DataFusion query support,
idempotent import, and the 16-capture fail-closed limit. The focused live API
test passed; `pnpm run verify:interface` passed 34 checks; touched Rust files
passed formatting and Clippy; `scripts/verify_imports.py` and `git diff
--check` passed. The UI action is source-verified but was not exercised in a
browser session. Reviewer status is `NOT_REQUESTED`; reproduction status is
`NOT_REPRODUCED`.

Data and artifact custody: GPUDiff source bytes and receipts existed only in
the disposable test home and were removed. Repository changes contain the
importer, tests, and documentation only. Known limitations: the feed is an
aggregator's public snapshot; provider fields and timestamps are publisher
claims. The test queried five rows and does not qualify price
representativeness, current capacity, direct provider access, or the browser
interaction. Claim ceiling remains source-attributed public records and
publisher timestamps only. The next blocked authority gates are scheduled
refresh, direct provider access, market/quote use, paid execution, public
publication, and production deployment; each requires a separately named
slice and authority.

## `hyperai.bazaar.gpudiff_owner_scheduled_refresh.v1`

Status: owner-controlled recurring import implemented and live in the local
owner service as of 2026-10-06 13:49 UTC. The schedule is volatile and stops
when that service stops. This is a continuation of
`hyperai.bazaar.gpudiff_live_offer_snapshot.v1`; it does not authorize direct
provider access, use as an executable offer, compute execution, payment,
publication, or production deployment.

Purpose: let the local owner start and stop a recurring refresh from the Data
workspace and inspect its status. Starting performs one immediate fixed-source
HTTPS GET and then polls every six hours while this local service process is
running. The schedule is volatile and stops when the owner stops it or the
service shuts down; restart never silently resumes network activity.

Exact writable files:

- `crates/hyperai-local-service/src/server.rs`: fixed-cadence scheduler,
  owner-only start/stop/status routes, bounded refresh reuse, and graceful
  scheduler shutdown.
- `crates/hyperai-data/src/lib.rs` and
  `crates/hyperai-data/tests/gpudiff_snapshot_contract.rs`: expose the
  existing capture-capacity stop as a distinct typed outcome and preserve its
  fail-closed contract.
- `crates/hyperai-local-service/tests/data_api.rs`: owner authorization,
  status transitions, scheduler start/stop, and live scheduled import/query
  coverage.
- `scripts/verify-interface-browser.mjs`: an explicit opt-in browser workflow
  for the real owner-started refresh, local catalog query, and owner stop.
- `apps/hyperai-interface/app.js`: explicit owner controls and schedule
  status in the Data workspace.
- `apps/hyperai-interface/index.html`: distinguish a local GPUDiff snapshot
  from synthetic-only data and clarify that no direct provider connection is
  active.
- `docs/compute-bazaar-route-auth-effect-inventory-v1.md`: inventory the
  three owner-only schedule routes and their remote-read/local-write effects;
  keep ACP/MCP's allowlist unchanged.
- `docs/compute-bazaar-gpudiff-live-offer-packet-v1.md`: exact schedule
  contract and end-to-end evidence.
- `docs/state-slices.md`: this scope and evidence record.

Allowed effects: the authenticated local owner may start one six-hour
schedule against only `https://gpudiff.com/api/v1/offers.json`. Each attempt
has the existing ten-second deadline, no redirect, no automatic retry, a
4 MiB body ceiling, and writes only digest-bound public source bytes,
normalized snapshot, and receipt beneath the selected HyperAI data root.
Transient failures preserve the currently cataloged snapshot and wait for
the next scheduled tick; they do not trigger an immediate retry. The schedule
retains the existing maximum of 16 distinct captures. At capacity it stops
without deleting or replacing evidence and reports the capacity stop. An
owner stop request takes effect after any in-flight request (bounded by the
ten-second deadline). Manual refresh remains available.

Non-goals: polling while HyperAI is closed; system or cloud daemons; source
webhooks or subscriptions; changing source terms, retention capacity, or
deletion behavior; direct provider APIs or credentials; GPU/H100 work;
normalizing publisher rows into executable market offers; quote/dispatch,
paid execution, settlement, external publication, or deployment.

Proof gates: focused tests must establish unauthenticated denial, owner-only
access, idempotent start, observable status, owner stop, bounded interval,
capacity stop, no deletion on capacity, and unchanged ACP/MCP route
capabilities. A live API and browser test must start through owner controls,
observe a non-empty current catalog entry with matching raw and normalized
digests, run bounded DataFusion SQL against that entry, stop the schedule, and
remove only the temporary test home. The real feed body must not enter the
repository or test output.

Claim ceiling: a locally retained sequence of GPUDiff-attributed public
snapshots with publisher-provided fields and timestamps. It does not prove
direct provider access, live capacity, provider endorsement, price
representativeness, computation correctness, buyer eligibility, payment
entitlement, or production readiness. Expected assurance is `INTERNAL_PASS`
for this local owner-controlled schedule and import/query path only; reviewer
status `NOT_REQUESTED`; reproduction status `NOT_REPRODUCED`.

Publish boundary: local owner-controlled source/data only, with visible
`gpudiff.com` CC BY 4.0 attribution. No public release or external
publication.

prompts under the recorded Codex CLI and hosted GPT-6 Luna configuration. A
response resembling a trace is not evidence that it matches internal

## `hyperai.demo.live_price_board_static_export.v1`

Status: implemented and locally qualified; hosted deployment is operator-run.

Purpose: let a public site show the existing live GPUDiff price snapshot
without exposing the owner-only HyperAI service.

Exact files: `demo/live-board/export.mjs`, `demo/live-board/export.test.mjs`,
`demo/live-board/site/{index.html,board.css,board.js,board.test.mjs}`,
`deploy/rpi5/*`, `package.json` (`test:demo` script), `.gitignore`, this record.
No Rust source, import digest, or existing product behavior changes.

Allowed effects: the exporter connects only to the recorded IPv4 loopback
address with the local owner bearer; it may call the existing fixed
`/api/v1/data/gpudiff/refresh` route (one GET to
`https://gpudiff.com/api/v1/offers.json`, no credentials), the catalog route,
and one fixed read-only data query; it atomically writes one static
`live-board.json`. The static site fetches only that same-origin file and
renders every string with `textContent`. Deployment notes for a Raspberry Pi 5
are unverified on hardware.

Non-goals: any public listener on the HyperAI service; exposing refresh,
schedule, deal, fleet, eval, trade, agent, or storage routes; authentication
changes; provider calls, purchases, orders, settlement, HIP-4 publication;
other data sources; forecasts or returns; production, security, SOTA, or
independent-verification claims.

Proof gates: `corepack pnpm run test:demo` (9 tests: row validation, https-only
sources, snapshot-digest binding, loopback-only fetches with bearer, atomic
write, non-loopback refusal, stale-data warning, no-HTML-injection rendering).
Manual: live refresh against the pinned service returned 2,581 feed rows and 53
valid GPU hourly rows.

Claim ceiling: source-attributed public list prices from an aggregator feed with
publisher timestamps (the dataset's own ceiling), shown read-only. Not an
executable offer, quote, capacity, or return. The service's query response
still labels results "synthetic local query result only"; the exporter uses the
catalog's GPUDiff ceiling and does not repeat that label.

Publish boundary: code and docs only; generated `live-board.json` is ignored.
